BARREL 4C data processing unit controlling instrument operations and acquiring X-ray spectrometer, magnetometer, GPS, and engineering telemetry during stratospheric balloon flight

BARREL Balloon 2D DPU (Data Processing Unit) platform data-handling unit acquiring and formatting X-ray spectrometer, magnetometer, Global Positioning System position/time, and engineering-interface telemetry for payload 2D of the second BARREL Antarctic balloon campaign (2013-2014), with data relayed through Iridium and command/cutdown control support

BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2D EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform product providing trajectory positions for payload 2D of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign (2013-2014), including balloon location in multiple geophysical coordinate systems for conjunction studies with radiation-belt observations

GOES-10 (1998–2009) Ephemeris platform position data product for the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 10 spacecraft, providing spacecraft geocentric/geostationary location, orbital longitude, orbit information, and time-tagged position vectors as ancillary context rather than a particle, field, or photon science sensor.

GOES-13 (2010–2017) EPS (Energetic Particle Sensor), energetic particle monitor on the GOES-N/GOES-13 spacecraft launched 2006 for Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites, measuring geosynchronous electrons, protons, and alpha particles; comprises MAGED (Magnetospheric Electron Detector), MAGPD (Magnetospheric Proton Detector), EPEAD (Energetic Proton, Electron, and Alpha Detector), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector), covering e− 30 keV->4 MeV, p+ 80 keV->700 MeV, α 3.8->3400 MeV

CANOPUS MPA (Meridian Photometer Array) ground-based meridian-scanning photometer array measuring auroral optical emissions and high-latitude ionospheric precipitation along magnetic meridians; four MSPs (meridian scanning photometers) on the ~337° and ~313° magnetic-longitude chains observed filtered auroral lines including Hβ 486.1 nm, OI 557.7/630.0 nm, and blue N2+/N2 bands near 427.8-470.9 nm

Cluster-Rumba WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric and magnetic plasma-wave waveforms and spectra in selected bands from 25 Hz to 577 kHz, using one selectable input from the Electric Field and Wave double-probe antennas or Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations search-coil magnetic sensors By/Bz for Cluster interferometric wave studies

Cluster-Salsa WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric and magnetic plasma-wave waveforms and spectra in selected bands from 25 Hz to 577 kHz in Earth’s magnetosphere; part of the WEC (Wave Experiments Consortium), using EFW (Electric Field and Wave) electric-antenna inputs and STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil inputs for spin-plane By or spin-axis Bz fields

Cluster-Tango Ephemeris spacecraft ephemeris data product measuring the Cluster 4/Tango spacecraft position and orbit state vectors in geocentric coordinate systems such as GSE, GSM and related mission coordinates; identifies the platform location for contextualizing Cluster field and plasma observations, not a science sensor itself

Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR) FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the interplanetary magnetic-field vector at L1 with <0.1 nT sensitivity and up to 0.02 s cadence; one of the PlasMag (Plasma Magnetometer) suite sensors alongside the Faraday Cup ion detector and top-hat electron electrostatic analyzer.

Dynamics Explorer 2 Ephemeris spacecraft-position ancillary platform data providing time-tagged DE-2 location along its low-altitude polar orbit in multiple coordinate systems, used to identify spacecraft altitude, latitude/longitude, invariant or magnetic latitude, magnetic local time, and conjunction geometry for DE-2 measurements

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2O EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product measuring the payload trajectory: time-tagged balloon position, latitude, longitude, and altitude in geographic and space-physics coordinate systems for unit 2O of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign, 2013-2014.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2M DPU (Data Processing Unit) payload avionics platform acquiring, time-tagging, and framing XRI (X-ray Instrument) bremsstrahlung spectra, magnetometer field data, GPS position/time, and EDI (Engineering Data Interface) housekeeping for Iridium downlink and cutdown control on payload 2M of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign (2013-2014)

Equator-S MAM (Magnetic Field Instrument) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic field strength and direction in the equatorial magnetosphere and solar wind; uses outboard and inboard sensors on a short boom to monitor spacecraft fields, with 16-bit data at 128 vectors/s for one sensor or 64 vectors/s for both and selectable ranges from ±250 to ±64000 nT

instruments.description: BARREL 3A tilt-compensated three-axis magnetometer measuring local magnetic field variations and ULF wave activity during stratospheric balloon flight

CLASP2 (Chromospheric LAyer SpectroPolarimeter 2) Spectropolarimeter2 sounding-rocket ultraviolet slit spectropolarimeter measuring full-Stokes I,Q,U,V solar chromospheric spectra around 279.4-280.7 nm, targeting Mg II k 279.64 nm, Mg II h 280.35 nm and nearby Mn I blends, with slit-jaw context imaging for coalignment

ChroTel ChroTel (Chromospheric Telescope) ground-based full-disk solar imaging telescope measuring chromospheric and transition-region solar intensity, morphology, and Doppler signatures in Ca II K 393.4 nm, H-alpha 656.3 nm, and He I 1083.0 nm narrowband channels, used for filaments, plages, active regions, and coronal-hole context

instruments.instrument_name: Full longwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (2007 flight)
instruments.description: EUNIS-2007 LW (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph long-wavelength channel) sounding-rocket normal-incidence EUV imaging spectrograph measuring full-Sun solar transition-region and coronal emission-line spectra in the longwave band, about 300–370 Å, during the 2007 EUNIS flight; counterpart to the EUNIS shortwave channel used for EUV radiometric calibration and line diagnostics

instruments.instrument_name: Full longwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (trimmed/2006 flight)
instruments.description: EUNIS-06 EUNIS (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph) sounding-rocket normal-incidence solar EUV imaging spectrograph measuring spatially resolved coronal and transition-region emission-line spectra; 2006 flight channels comprise the LW longwave band (300-370 Å, including full/trimmed LW solar observations) and the SW shortwave band (170-205 Å) for irradiance and cross-calibration

instruments.instrument_name: Full longwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (trimmed/2007 flight)
instruments.description: EUNIS 2007 flight EUNIS (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph) sounding-rocket normal-incidence EUV imaging spectrograph measuring solar transition-region and coronal line radiance spectra; this record is the trimmed full LW (long-wavelength) channel observation in ~300-370 Å, with the contemporaneous SW (short-wavelength) channel covering ~170-205 Å

instruments.mission_name: Osservatorio Astrofisico di Catania, Via S.Sofia 78, 95123 Catania ITALY
instruments.description: Osservatorio Astrofisico di Catania BE-Halpha (Birefringent-filter Hydrogen-alpha) narrowband solar telescope/imager measuring full-disk chromospheric H-alpha line-center intensity at 656.28 nm, used for Catania H-alpha patrol images of filaments, plages, prominences, and flares with a Lyot/birefringent filter bandpass of about 0.25 Å

Cluster-Samba (SC3) STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetometer and spectrum-analyzer wave instrument measuring AC magnetic and electric field fluctuations and electromagnetic wave spectral matrices; comprising STAFF-SC waveform/search-coil data (0.1–10 Hz normal, 0.1–180 Hz burst) and STAFF-SA spectral matrices using three magnetic plus two electric components over 8 Hz–4 kHz

Cluster-Salsa (SC2) STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetometer and wave spectrum analyzer measuring three-axis AC magnetic and electric field fluctuations and wave spectral matrices in the Cluster WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium), providing B waveforms at 0.1-10 Hz or 0.1-180 Hz and STAFF-SA spectra using 3 magnetic plus 2 EFW (Electric Field and Wave) components from ~8/64 Hz to 4 kHz

Cluster-Samba (SC3) PEACE (Plasma Electron and Current Experiment) dual electrostatic electron spectrometer measuring 3-D electron velocity distribution functions, moments, pitch-angle distributions, and currents in the magnetosphere and solar wind; comprising LEEA (low-energy electron analyzer) and HEEA (high-energy electron analyzer), covering 0.6 eV-26 keV / ~0.67 eV-30 keV in 92 energy steps

GOES-13 (2010–2017) Ephemeris spacecraft platform data product providing position and orbit/geostationary trajectory information for heliophysics context, including time-tagged geocentric location, longitude/latitude/altitude or Cartesian coordinates used to place GOES-13 particle, X-ray, EUV, and magnetic-field observations in space and time

GOES-7 (1987–1996) Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 7 EPM (Energetic Particle Monitor), energetic particle monitor measuring geostationary proton, alpha-particle, and electron fluxes in 25 channels: protons in seven bands from 0.8–500 MeV plus HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector) proton channels >370 MeV, alpha particles from 4 to >400 MeV and >640 MeV/nucleon, and electrons >500 keV

instruments.instrument_name: The Solar Upper Transition Region Imager
instruments.description: SATech-01 SUTRI (Solar Upper Transition Region Imager) extreme-ultraviolet solar telescope measuring full-disk upper-transition-region EUV emission in the Ne VII 46.5 nm (465 Å) passband, sensitive to ~0.5 MK plasma, providing solar-disk and low-corona images used for transition-region dynamics, eruptions, coronal holes, and solar activity studies.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1S XRI (X-ray Instrument) sodium iodide scintillator spectrometer measuring bremsstrahlung X-ray flux and spectra from precipitating radiation-belt electrons; payload 1S of the first Antarctic campaign (2012-2013), with 10 keV-10 MeV response, 50 ms rates in 10-180, 180-550, 550-840, and 840-1500 keV bands, plus spectra over 20 keV-7 MeV

Yohkoh SXT (Soft X-Ray Telescope) grazing-incidence soft-X-ray imaging telescope measuring solar coronal and flare X-ray brightness, morphology, temperature, and emission measure in broadband filter images over ~0.25-4 keV (~3-50 Å), from full-Sun context to high-cadence active-region and flare observations

Yohkoh WBS (Wide Band Spectrometer) solar X-ray and gamma-ray spectrometer suite measuring flare spectra and high-energy light curves from ~2 keV to ~100 MeV; comprising SXS (Soft X-ray Spectrometer, ~2-30 keV), HXS (Hard X-ray Spectrometer, ~20-400 keV), GRS (Gamma-Ray Spectrometer, ~0.2-100 MeV) and RBM (Radiation Belt Monitor, particle/background rates).

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1I EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform product measuring balloon trajectory position versus time for payload 1I of the first Antarctic campaign (2012-2013), providing location and altitude in multiple coordinate systems for conjunction studies with radiation-belt observations

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1T EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform product providing trajectory positions, altitude, latitude/longitude, and magnetic/geocentric coordinate locations for payload 1T of the first Antarctic balloon campaign (2012-2013), used to contextualize X-ray observations and Van Allen Probes conjunctions.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1K EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product providing reconstructed trajectory positions, altitude, latitude, longitude, and coordinate-system transforms for payload 1K of the first Antarctic BARREL campaign (2012-2013), used to locate its X-ray measurements conjugate to the Van Allen Probes
AeroCube-6A Dosimeter
AeroCube-6B Dosimeter

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1S DPU (Data Processing Unit) payload data-processing platform measuring no science quantities directly but acquiring and framing XRI (X-ray Instrument) 10 keV-10 MeV spectra/count rates, magnetometer, GPS (Global Positioning System), and EDI (Engineering Data Interface) housekeeping data; payload 1S of the first Antarctic campaign (2012-2013)

LANL Spacecraft Series LANL-02A/LANL 2002 (2002–2008) MPA (Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer measuring three-dimensional ion and electron energy-per-charge distributions in geosynchronous magnetospheric plasma (~1 eV/q to >40 keV/q), with spin-swept nearly full-sky angular coverage for moments and distribution functions

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1U XRI (X-ray instrument) NaI scintillator spectrometer measuring bremsstrahlung X-ray flux and spectra from precipitating radiation-belt electrons; payload 1U of the first Antarctic campaign (2012-2013), with 10 keV-10 MeV response, 50 ms bands at 10-180, 180-550, 550-840, 840-1500 keV, and 20 keV-7 MeV spectra

BARREL Balloon 1H MAG (Magnetometer) tilt-compensated three-axis PNI TCM2-20 magnetometer measuring vector magnetic-field components at 1 s cadence with ~10 nT resolution, used for substorm and ultra-low-frequency (ULF) wave context for X-ray precipitation; payload 1H of the first BARREL Antarctic balloon campaign (2012-2013)

AMPTE/CCE MEPA (Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers/Charge Composition Explorer Medium Energy Particle Analyzer) energetic-particle time-of-flight mass spectrometer measuring magnetospheric and tracer-ion spectra, composition, and angular distributions from ~10 keV/nucleon for O to >6 MeV; resolves H and He isotopes, elements through O, and major species/groups beyond Fe with 32-sector angular resolution and 0.2-24 s cadence.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1C EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product measuring time-tagged trajectory positions and balloon location in multiple coordinate systems for payload 1C of the first Antarctic BARREL campaign, 2012-2013

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1H EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform product measuring/providing payload trajectory positions, altitude, and derived locations in geographic, geocentric, and geomagnetic coordinate systems for payload 1H of the first Antarctic balloon campaign (2012-2013).

Alouette 2 SFS (Sweep-Frequency Sounder) topside ionosonde measuring ionospheric electron density, virtual range, plasma resonances, birefringence and propagation effects by transmitting swept RF pulses from 0.12 to 14.5 MHz every 32 s and recording echo delay times, extending topside soundings over ~300-3000 km altitude.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1U EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform/trajectory product measuring payload 1U position and altitude versus time, with balloon coordinates supplied in geographic, geocentric, and geomagnetic systems for payload 1U of the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014).

BARREL Balloon 1K MAG (Magnetometer) TCM2 tilt-compensated three-axis magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic-field components at 1 s cadence with ~10–50 nT resolution, used to identify substorm activity and ULF magnetic-field oscillations during BARREL Antarctic campaign 1 (2012–2013) on payload 1K.

GOES-16 (2017–present) (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 16) SUVI (Solar Ultraviolet Imager) normal-incidence extreme-ultraviolet solar telescope on the GOES-R Series platform, observing full-disk solar atmosphere, chromosphere, transition-region, and coronal emission for flare and space-weather monitoring in six passbands: 94, 131, 171, 195, 284, and 304 Å

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1M EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product measuring/reporting trajectory positions for payload 1M of the first Antarctic BARREL campaign (2012-2013), providing balloon location in geographic and space-physics coordinate systems for conjunction studies with the XRI X-ray instrument and Van Allen Probes

BARREL Balloon 1V EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform product providing the trajectory positions of BARREL payload 1V from the first Antarctic BARREL campaign (2012-2013), reporting balloon location and altitude in time-tagged geographic and geocentric coordinate systems for conjunction studies with radiation-belt observations

GOES-7 (1987–1996) MAG (Magnetic Field Monitor) spinning twin-fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-axis geomagnetic-field components at geostationary orbit: Hp (spin-axis/north-south), He (earthward), and Hn (eastward), with ~0.2 nT sensitivity; after May 1993 only Hp was usable with uncertain absolute level

ACE SEPICA (Solar Energetic Particle Ionic Charge Analyzer) electrostatic deflection/solid-state telescope measuring ionic charge state, kinetic energy, and nuclear charge of energetic ions above ~0.2 MeV/nucleon, targeting solar energetic particles, flare and shock ions, corotating interaction regions, and anomalous cosmic rays from the termination shock

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2B EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product giving time-tagged trajectory positions for payload 2B of the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), including balloon latitude, longitude, altitude, and positions in geocentric/geomagnetic coordinate systems for conjunction and context studies.

DMSP Series SESS/SSI/ES-3 (Special Sensor Ions, Electrons, and Scintillation-3), represented by DMSP F18 (2009–present), Langmuir-probe/plasma-drift suite measuring topside ionospheric electron density and temperature, ion density and temperature, mean ion mass, cross-track and along-track plasma drifts, and scintillation; comprising Langmuir Probe, Retarding Potential Analyzer, Ion Drift Meter, and Scintillation Meter sensors.

BARREL Balloon 2N XRI (X-ray Instrument), a NaI scintillator spectrometer measuring bremsstrahlung X-ray spectra and flux from precipitating radiation-belt electrons over 10 keV-10 MeV; payload 2N of the second BARREL Antarctic balloon campaign (2013-2014), with 50 ms bands at 10-180, 180-550, 550-840, and 840-1500 keV plus 20 keV-7 MeV spectra in 48 channels at 4 s and 256 channels at 32 s

Cluster-Samba (SC3) WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of Electron density by Relaxation) active relaxation sounder/passive electric-field wave receiver measuring total/cold electron density (~0.2-80 cm^-3) and high-frequency plasma/electric-field wave spectra from 4-80 kHz, using Electric Field and Wave (EFW) double-sphere antennas in the Cluster Wave Experiment Consortium with STAFF, WBD and DWP.

Cluster-Samba EFW (Electric Field and Waves) long-wire double-probe instrument measuring spin-plane electric fields, waveforms, spacecraft potential, and probe-derived plasma density/temperature; four spherical probes on two orthogonal wire-boom pairs provide field products from direct current to 10 Hz, 180 Hz, 4 kHz, or 32 kHz, wave fields from 10 Hz–8 kHz, and a 10–200 kHz counter.

Cluster-Rumba WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of Electron density by Relaxation) double-sphere active plasma sounder and passive high-frequency wave receiver in the Cluster Wave Experiment Consortium, measuring total local electron density including cold plasma (~0.2-80 cm⁻³) from resonances and natural electric-field emissions over 4-80 kHz using the EFW antenna system

Dynamics Explorer 2 NACS (Neutral Atmosphere Composition Spectrometer) quadrupole mass spectrometer measuring in situ neutral thermospheric composition and constituent densities from 0-51 amu at 0.2 amu mass steps, including major species such as O, N2, O2, He, and Ar, with baffle scans for zonal and vertical neutral wind signatures in composition variations

Deep Space Climate Observatory DSCOVR (Deep Space Climate Observatory) PlasMag (Plasma-Magnetometer) FC (Faraday Cup) solar wind positive-ion detector measuring 3-D proton/alpha bulk moments—density, velocity, flow direction, temperature and dynamic pressure—at up to 0.5 s cadence near L1; one PlasMag sensor alongside the MAG fluxgate vector magnetometer and ES (Electron Spectrometer) top-hat analyzer

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2Q XRI (X-ray Instrument) NaI scintillator spectrometer measuring bremsstrahlung X-ray flux and spectra from precipitating radiation-belt electrons, 10 keV-10 MeV, with 50 ms rates in 10-180, 180-550, 550-840, 840-1500 keV bands and 20 keV-7 MeV spectra; payload 2Q of the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014)

ELFIN-B (Electron Losses and Fields Investigation B) EPD (Energetic Particle Detector) solid-state energetic-particle telescope suite measuring spin-resolved trapped and precipitating radiation-belt electrons and ions, pitch-angle distributions, spectra, and fluxes; comprising EPDE (Energetic Particle Detector for Electrons, ~50 keV–5 MeV) and EPDI (Energetic Particle Detector for Ions, ~250 keV–5 MeV) on the ELFIN B CubeSat

Genesis GIM-GEM (Genesis Plasma Spectrometers) electrostatic analyzer suite measuring solar wind plasma for sample-collector state selection and science distributions, comprising GIM (Genesis Ion Monitor) ion E/q analyzer covering ~100 eV-14 keV and GEM (Genesis Electron Monitor) electron analyzer covering 1-1400 eV at L1

Cluster-Samba CIS (Cluster Ion Spectrometry) ion spectrometer suite measuring full three-dimensional ion velocity distributions, moments, and mass-per-charge composition each spin; comprising HIA (Hot Ion Analyzer), covering ~5 eV/q–32 keV/q, and CODIF (Composition and Distribution Function analyzer), resolving H+, He++, He+, and O+ from spacecraft potential/~20 eV/q to 40 keV/q

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2I DPU (Data Processing Unit) payload data-system platform acquiring and framing XRI (X-ray Instrument) spectra, magnetometer, GPS (Global Positioning System), and EDI (Engineering Data Interface) housekeeping measurements for the 2I Antarctic campaign balloon payload in 2013-2014, with command/cutdown control and Iridium downlink formatting

BepiColombo Ephemeris (spacecraft positions) virtual platform product providing BepiColombo spacecraft state vectors—position, velocity, trajectory, and observing geometry for the MPO (Mercury Planetary Orbiter), Mio/MMO (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter), and cruise stack—used to locate fields-and-particles measurements in heliocentric, planetary, and Mercury-centered coordinates

Galileo Ephemeris platform ephemeris data product reporting the Galileo spacecraft time-tagged position and velocity state vectors for observation geometry, timing, and coordinate transformations during interplanetary cruise and the Jupiter tour; not a science sensor but the mission trajectory/positions context record.

CANOPUS MARI (Magnetometer and Riometer Array) ground-based magnetometer/riometer network measuring auroral-zone magnetic perturbations, pulsations, electrojet currents, and ionospheric cosmic-noise absorption; comprising three-component fluxgate magnetometer stations and colocated/broad-beam riometers, typically at 30 MHz, used in ISTP/GGS high-latitude studies

DMSP Series SESS/SSJ5; DMSP F17 (2006–2022), Defense Meteorological Satellite Program Flight 17 Block 5D-3 launched 2006, SSJ5 (Special Sensor Precipitating Electron and Ion Spectrometer 5) electrostatic spectrometer measuring precipitating electron/ion differential and energy flux in 19 fixed channels from ~30/50 eV to 30 keV; a Space Environment Sensor Suite sensor alongside SSIES and SSM

Cassini MAG (Magnetometer) dual-sensor magnetometer measuring vector magnetic field and absolute field magnitude at Saturn, in the solar wind, and during planetary flybys; comprising the FGM (fluxgate magnetometer) and the VHM/SHM (vector helium magnetometer/scalar helium magnetometer), covering sub-nT fields to tens of thousands of nT

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2X EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product providing trajectory positions rather than particle measurements, giving the Balloon 2X payload location in multiple coordinate systems for the second Antarctic BARREL campaign (2013-2014) and enabling conjunction studies with Van Allen Probes and ground stations

NOAA-7 SEM (Space Environment Monitor) energetic particle suite measuring upper-atmosphere, radiation-belt and solar-particle electron, proton and alpha fluxes; comprising TED (total energy detector, 300 eV-20 keV electrons/protons), MEPED (medium-energy proton and electron detector: protons 30 keV->2.5 MeV, electrons >30/>100/>300 keV, mixed >6 MeV, omni protons >16/>36/>80 MeV) and HEPAT/HEPAD high-energy proton-alpha telescope/detector (>370 MeV protons, >850 MeV/nucleon alphas)

Giotto Ephemeris (Giotto Positions) platform ephemeris data product providing the Giotto spacecraft trajectory, position, and timing context in heliocentric/geocentric coordinates for interpreting in situ plasma, fields, dust, and neutral-gas measurements during the ESA Halley-comet flyby mission

Kilpisjarvi Geophysical Observatory ASC (All Sky Camera) all-sky optical imager measuring broadband visible auroral luminosity, color morphology, and sky distribution over Kilpisjärvi using fisheye hemispheric imaging; cited as the Kilpisjärvi all-sky camera for contextual auroral forms, arcs, breakup, and optical conjugacy studies.

Cluster-Tango FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the direct-current vector magnetic field in the terrestrial magnetosphere and solar wind; the Cluster 4/Tango unit uses inboard and outboard boom sensors, selectable ranges from about ±64/±256 nT to ±65,536 nT, and delivers spin, normal high-resolution (~22 vectors/s) and burst (~67 vectors/s) data.

Cluster-Rumba PEACE (Plasma Electron and Current Experiment) electron electrostatic analyzer suite measuring three-dimensional thermal plasma electron velocity distributions, moments, currents, pitch-angle distributions and spacecraft potential from 0.67 eV to 30 keV; comprising LEEA (low-energy electron analyzer) and HEEA (high-energy electron analyzer) sensors.

MMS-4 EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) electron drift instrument measuring convection electric field and magnetic-field magnitude from the drift/return of coded ~1 keV electron beams; part of the MMS-4 FIELDS suite alongside AFG (Analog Fluxgate), DFG (Digital Fluxgate), SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), and ADP (Axial Double Probe).

IBEX Hi (high-energy energetic neutral atom camera) neutral atom imager measuring energetic neutral atoms (ENAs) from the outer heliosphere in six energy bands, band 1-6: 0.38-0.59, 0.52-0.95, 0.84-1.55, 1.36-2.50, 1.99-3.75, and 3.13-6.00 keV, complementing the IBEX Lo sensor for lower-energy ENA sky maps

SuperDARN (Super Dual Auroral Radar Network) HF coherent-scatter radar network measuring ionospheric field-aligned irregularity backscatter at ~8-20 MHz to derive line-of-sight plasma drift velocity, echo power, spectral width, convection/electric fields, polar cap potential, and neutral-wind/meteor-trail parameters across high-, polar-, and mid-latitudes

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2L EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product providing trajectory positions rather than particle or X-ray measurements; payload 2L of the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), with time-tagged balloon latitude, longitude, altitude, and magnetic/space-physics coordinates for conjunction studies

LANL Spacecraft Series LANL 1991 (1991–2008) MPA (Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer measuring three-dimensional geosynchronous plasma ion and electron energy-per-charge distributions from ~1 eV/q to >40 keV/q, individual Los Alamos National Laboratory spacecraft-series unit cited as LANL-1991 or 1991-080 MPA

Cluster-Salsa EFW (Electric Field and Waves) long-wire double-probe instrument measuring spin-plane direct-current (DC) and alternating-current (AC) electric fields, waveforms, spacecraft potential and probe-derived plasma density/temperature; four spherical probes on two 100 m tip-to-tip wire booms, covering DC fields to 10 Hz/180 Hz/4 kHz/32 kHz, AC 10 Hz-8 kHz, density fluctuations to 4 kHz and a 10-200 kHz frequency counter

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2T DPU (Data Processing Unit) platform controller supporting balloon X-ray and magnetic-field measurements by acquiring and framing XRI (X-ray instrument, 10 keV-10 MeV), magnetometer, GPS (Global Positioning System), and EDI (Engineering Data Interface) data for Iridium downlink and command cutdown; unit 2T, second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014)

GOES-11 (2006–2011; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 11, prelaunch GOES-L) Ephemeris platform data product providing spacecraft position and orbit information for the GOES I-M geostationary fleet/GOES mission, launched in 2000 and used for heliophysics context as a geocentric/geostationary observing location, including longitude, radius, and time-tagged orbital position rather than particle or field measurements

Parker Solar Probe V3 (Voltage Probe 3) electric-field antenna measuring spacecraft-to-probe potential and contributing to DC/AC electric-field, quasi-thermal-noise, and radio/plasma-wave observations; one of the FIELDS (Fields Experiment) voltage sensors alongside V1, V2, V4 sunlit probes and the V5 boom-mounted probe

IBEX-Lo (Interstellar Boundary Explorer Low Energy) neutral atom imager measuring low-energy energetic neutral atom (ENA) sky maps, composition, and angular fluxes from ~0.01-2.0 keV; a single-pixel imager with 7°×7° and high-resolution 3.5°×3.5° fields of view, bands 1-8 centered at 14, 27, 52, 102, 197, 451, 908, and 1903 eV, and triple-coincidence time-of-flight mass analysis for H, O, and He ENAs

GOES-11 (2006–2011) SEM (Space Environment Monitor) space-weather instrument suite measuring geosynchronous magnetic fields, solar soft X-ray flux, and energetic particle fluxes; comprising MFS (Magnetic Field Sensor, ±1000 nT), XRS (Solar X-ray Sensor, 0.5–5 Å and 1–8 Å), EPS (Energetic Particle Sensor, protons 0.8–500 MeV), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector, protons >350 MeV and alpha particles >640 MeV/nucleon)

GOES-13 (2010–2017) MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring local geostationary geomagnetic-field magnitude, vector components, field vector, and magnetic-field variations for sudden impulses, magnetopause crossings, and geomagnetic activity; GOES-N/O/P generation unit GOES-13/GOES-N, launched 2006 and used as GOES-East 2010–2017, with primary and backup boom-mounted sensors.

ISEE-3 Ephemeris (International Sun-Earth Explorer 3 spacecraft position) platform ephemeris data product reporting the spacecraft position vector in GSE (Geocentric Solar Ecliptic) coordinates for contextualizing ISEE-3 heliospheric, magnetospheric, and solar-wind measurements, not a particle or field sensor

GOES-8 (1995–2003) EPM (Energetic Particle Monitor) energetic particle instrument measuring geostationary solar energetic and trapped proton, alpha-particle, and electron fluxes, including >2 MeV electrons; comprising the EP8 Telescope, Dome Assembly, and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector), with P1–P11 proton channels (~0.8 to >700 MeV) and A1–A8 alpha channels (few to ~1000 MeV/nucleon).

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2P EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual instrument measuring the 2P payload trajectory/position for the second BARREL Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), providing time-tagged latitude, longitude, altitude and derived geographic, geomagnetic, L-shell and magnetic-local-time coordinates for locating X-ray precipitation observations

Geotail SWA (Solar Wind Analyzer) quadrispherical electrostatic plasma analyzer measuring three-dimensional solar-wind ion fluxes, velocity distributions, and moments over 150-7,000 eV/q; a sensor of the CPI (Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation) suite alongside the HPA (Hot Plasma Analyzer) for hot magnetospheric plasma

POLAR MFE (Magnetic Fields Experiment) fluxgate magnetometer measuring the local vector DC magnetic field in Earth’s polar magnetosphere; dual triaxial boom-mounted fluxgate sensors, outboard and inboard for spacecraft-field removal, provide redundant measurements over selectable ranges of about ±700, ±5700, and ±47,000 nT.

Dynamics Explorer 2 IDM (Ion Drift Meter) ion drift instrument measuring thermal ion arrival angles and bulk ionospheric plasma flow perpendicular to the spacecraft velocity, reported as horizontal and vertical ion-drift velocities (±4 km/s, 1/32-s cadence) for convection/electric-field studies; comprising SDS (standard drift sensor) and UDS (universal drift sensor).

Geotail LEP (Low Energy Particle Experiment) quadrispherical electrostatic analyzer suite measuring low-energy plasma and energetic ions/electrons in the magnetotail and solar wind; comprising LEP-EA (Energy-per-charge Analyzer) with EA-e and EA-i electron/ion analyzers for 3-D distributions from several eV/q to 43 keV/q, LEP-SW (Solar Wind ion analyzer), and LEP-MS (energetic-ion Mass Spectrometer, failed shortly after launch)

Cluster-Salsa DWP (Digital Wave Processor) wave-processing and WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium) coordination instrument producing timing, compression, and particle-correlation products for wave/particle studies from DC to >100 kHz; one of the five WEC instruments alongside EFW (Electric Field and Wave), STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations), WBD (Wide Band Data), and WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing Electron density by Relaxation).

Geotail PWI (Plasma Wave Investigation) plasma wave receiver suite measuring electric and magnetic field spectra and waveforms in the magnetotail; comprising SFA (Sweep Frequency Analyzer), MCA (Multi-Channel Analyzer) and WFC (Wave-Form Capture), using WANT wire and PANT probe 100 m tip-to-tip electric dipoles plus triaxial search coils, with E-field 5.6 Hz-800 kHz, B-field 5.6 Hz-12.5 kHz and WFC 10 Hz-4 kHz

Karmoy Geophysical Observatory MAG (magnetometer) ground-based geomagnetic field instrument measuring three-component magnetic field variations (X/Y/Z or H/D/Z) at the Karmøy, Norway station, used for auroral electrojet, magnetic storm/substorm, Pc/ULF pulsation, and ionospheric current studies.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2Y DPU (Data Processing Unit) balloon payload controller/data-system platform acquiring and framing X-ray spectrometer/XRI, magnetometer, GPS, and Engineering Data Interface housekeeping data for Iridium downlink and cutdown control; unit 2Y of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign (2013-2014)

PENGUIn-3 PG3 (Polar Experiment Network for Geospace Upper-atmosphere Investigations site 3) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations, magnetic pulsations, and auroral/substorm current signatures at the Antarctic PENGUIn-3 geophysical observatory station

Cluster-Rumba RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) energetic-particle imaging spectrometer measuring suprathermal electron, ion, and energetic neutral atom angular distributions; comprising IES (Imaging Electron Spectrometer, electrons ~20-400 keV) and IIMS (Imaging Ion Mass Spectrometer, ions ~2 keV/nucleon-1.5 MeV/nucleon, resolving protons, helium, and carbon-nitrogen-oxygen groups; neutrals ~10-100 keV)

Cluster-Samba FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the direct current vector magnetic field in Earth’s magnetosphere and solar wind; the Cluster C3/Samba unit uses inboard and outboard boom sensors with selectable ranges ±256 to ±65,536 nT, providing spin-resolution to ~20 vectors/s nominal and burst/high-rate data for boundary crossings and shocks

Dynamics Explorer 1 PWI (Plasma Waves Instrument) plasma-wave investigation measuring AC electric fields from 1 Hz to 2 MHz and magnetic fluctuations from 1 Hz to 400 kHz, covering extremely-low-frequency (ELF), very-low-frequency (VLF), and high-frequency (HF) waves such as auroral kilometric radiation, VLF hiss, and electrostatic waves.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2L MAG (Magnetometer) TCM2 tilt-compensated three-axis magnetometer measuring vector magnetic-field components at 1 s cadence with ~10 nT resolution for substorm and ULF-wave context during the second Antarctic BARREL campaign, 2013-2014

DMSP Series SESS/SSI/ES-3, as flown on DMSP F17 (2006–2022), Special Sensor for Ions, Electrons, and Scintillation, version 3, thermal plasma drift/scintillation suite and Langmuir/electron probe measuring in situ ionospheric ion/electron density and temperature, ion composition/mean molecular weight, plasma drift velocity, and electron-density scintillation at DMSP altitude; with Retarding Potential Analyzer, Ion Drift Meter, Langmuir/electron sensor, and scintillation meter

GOES-12 (2003–2010) (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 12) Ephemeris spacecraft-position platform data providing geostationary satellite location for heliophysics context, identifying the GOES-M flight unit used as GOES-East and later GOES-South America during the 2001–2013 GOES I–M era rather than an in situ particle or field sensor

Cluster-Salsa WHISPER (Waves of High frequency and Sounder for Probing Electron density by Relaxation) relaxation sounder and high-frequency electric-wave receiver measuring total/cold electron density (~0.2-80 cm^-3) from active plasma resonances and natural emissions at 4-80 kHz; Wave Experiment Consortium sensor alongside EFW (Electric Fields and Waves), STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) and WBD (Wide Band Data)

Cluster-Salsa RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) energetic particle imaging spectrometer measuring electrons (20-400 keV), ions (2 keV/nucleon-1.5 MeV/nucleon; protons, helium, carbon-nitrogen-oxygen groups), and energetic neutral atoms (10-100 keV); comprising IIMS (Imaging Ion Mass Spectrometer, three SCENIC [Spectroscopic Camera for Electrons, Neutral and Ion Composition] heads) and IES (Imaging Electron Spectrometer)

Geotail Ephemeris (spacecraft position) platform data product giving Geotail spacecraft location and trajectory relative to Earth for contextualizing plasma, field, and particle observations, with position vectors in common geocentric coordinate systems such as GSE, GSM, GEI, and SM rather than a science sensor measurement.

Cluster-Samba EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) electron-drift beam instrument measuring the convection electric field, cross-field drift, magnetic-field gradient drift, and magnetic-field magnitude by firing coded 0.5 and 1 keV test electron beams from two opposing gun-detector units and detecting their return after one gyroperiod on the Cluster-Samba spacecraft.

Equator-S Ephemeris spacecraft ephemeris/platform data product giving Equator-S spacecraft position and trajectory in geocentric solar-ecliptic, geocentric solar-magnetospheric, and related coordinate systems for locating magnetic-field, plasma, and wave observations in the near-equatorial magnetosphere

Cluster-Rumba Ephemeris spacecraft position data product providing the Cluster FM5/Rumba observatory location and orbit state vectors versus time in geocentric solar ecliptic (GSE), geocentric solar magnetospheric (GSM), solar magnetic (SM), geographic, and related coordinate systems; contextual auxiliary data, not a plasma or fields sensor.

Geotail MGF (Magnetic Field Experiment) magnetometer suite measuring vector magnetic fields and low-frequency magnetic fluctuations in the magnetotail, magnetosphere, and solar wind; comprising dual three-axis fluxgate magnetometers (FGM, ±16 to ±65536 nT ranges, 16 vectors/s) and a three-axis search-coil magnetometer (SCM, ~0.5–50 Hz class fluctuations)

Cluster-Salsa PEACE (Plasma Electron and Current Experiment) dual electrostatic analyzer measuring 3-D electron velocity distribution functions, density/velocity/temperature moments, pitch-angle distributions, and electron currents over 0.67 eV-30 keV; comprising LEEA (low-energy electron analyzer) and HEEA (high-energy electron analyzer) sensors

Cluster-Tango DWP (Digital Wave Processor) wave-processing and particle-correlator experiment measuring/deriving synchronized electric and magnetic wave data and particle-count autocorrelations from DC to >100 kHz; one of the WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium) instruments alongside EFW (Electric Fields and Waves), STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations), WBD (Wide Band Data) and WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of Electron density by Relaxation).

Cluster-Salsa (FM6, Flight Model 6) Ephemeris spacecraft-position data product providing the Salsa spacecraft position and orbit state vectors for Cluster tetrahedron analyses in geocentric solar ecliptic, geocentric solar magnetospheric, geocentric solar equatorial, geographic/geocentric equatorial, and magnetic coordinate systems

FAST MAG (Magnetometer) tri-axial fluxgate and search-coil magnetometer investigation measuring auroral-zone magnetic field vectors and fluctuations; comprising the DC fluxgate magnetometer for fields from DC to 100 Hz and the AC search-coil magnetometer for wave magnetic fields from 10 Hz to 2.5 kHz with high-time-resolution sampling

Cluster-Tango WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric and magnetic plasma-wave waveforms and spectra in selected bands from 25 Hz to 577 kHz; a Cluster Wave Experiments Consortium instrument using selectable EFW (Electric Field and Wave) electric-antenna inputs and STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetic inputs, including spin-plane and spin-axis components

Dynamics Explorer 1 EICS (Energetic Ion Composition Spectrometer) spectrometer measuring energetic ion composition, mass-per-charge, and energy-per-charge in the auroral acceleration region, cusp, and ring current; covers <1 to >150 amu/e in 64 mass channels with 32 energy-per-charge steps from ~0 to 17 keV/e and mass resolution M/ΔM >10 at focus

Cassini Ephemeris (Cassini Positions) platform data product providing the Cassini spacecraft position and trajectory versus time, used to locate observations during interplanetary cruise, Jupiter flyby, Saturn orbital tour, Titan and icy-satellite encounters, ring-plane crossings, and magnetospheric passes; not a physical science detector

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2N DPU (Data Processing Unit) payload controller/data-processing platform for payload 2N in the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), acquiring and framing XRI (X-Ray Instrument) NaI spectrometer, magnetometer, GPS (Global Positioning System), and EDI (Engineering Data Interface) housekeeping data for Iridium downlink and cutdown commanding

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2K EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform measuring payload trajectory positions rather than X-ray counts, providing time-tagged location/altitude in geographic and geomagnetic coordinate systems for payload 2K of the second Antarctic BARREL balloon campaign (2013-2014)

Geotail HPA (Hot Plasma Analyzer) quadrispherical electrostatic plasma analyzer of the CPI (Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation) suite measuring three-dimensional electron and ion differential fluxes, velocity distributions, densities, temperatures, and flows over ~1-50,000 eV/q in the terrestrial magnetosphere and solar wind

Cluster-Tango EFW (Electric Field and Waves) long-wire double-probe instrument measuring spin-plane electric fields (0.1-700 V/km; DC to 10 Hz, 180 Hz, 4 kHz or 32 kHz), AC fields (10 Hz-8 kHz; ~3 mV/km-10 V/km), plasma density fluctuations, spacecraft potential, and Langmuir-sweep density/temperature, using four spherical probes on two orthogonal wire-boom dipoles plus a 10-200 kHz frequency counter

BARREL Balloon 2L XRI (X-ray Instrument) NaI scintillator spectrometer measuring bremsstrahlung X-ray spectra and flux from precipitating radiation-belt electrons (10 keV-10 MeV); payload 2L of the second BARREL Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), with 50 ms bands at 10-180, 180-550, 550-840, and 840-1500 keV plus 4 s/48-channel and 32 s/256-channel spectra from 20 keV-7 MeV

GOES-6 (1983–1994) MAG (Magnetometer) biaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-axis geomagnetic field vectors at geostationary/geosynchronous orbit in Hp (spin-axis/north-south), He (earthward radial), and Hn (eastward) components; GOES-6 unit of the GOES-4–7 spin-stabilized series, with ±400 nT range, 0.1 nT resolution over ±50 nT, and ~0.2 nT sensitivity

Dynamics Explorer 1 DE-1 (Dynamics Explorer 1) Ephemeris platform trajectory product providing spacecraft position, altitude, latitude/longitude, local time, and magnetic/geomagnetic coordinates for the high-altitude polar orbiter, used to geolocate DE-1 field, plasma, auroral imaging, and wave observations rather than as a science detector

BARREL Balloon 2W DPU (Data Processing Unit), flight data system for Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses payload 2W of the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), acquiring and framing XRI (X-ray Instrument) spectrometer, magnetometer, GPS (Global Positioning System), and EDI (Engineering Data Interface) housekeeping data for Iridium downlink and cutdown control

Cluster-Tango RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) energetic particle imaging spectrometer measuring 3-D suprathermal electron (20-400 keV), ion (2 keV/nucleon-1.5 MeV/nucleon; protons, helium, carbon-nitrogen-oxygen group) and energetic neutral atom (10-100 keV) distributions; comprising IIMS (Imaging Ion Mass Spectrometer, three SCENIC heads) and IES (Imaging Electron Spectrometer)

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2Q EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product providing payload trajectory positions, latitude, longitude, altitude, and coordinate-system ephemerides for unit 2Q of the second Antarctic balloon campaign, 2013-2014, used to locate BARREL particle-precipitation X-ray observations

Equator-S SFD (Scintillating Fiber Detector) scintillation particle detector measuring energetic radiation-belt/magnetospheric electron and proton fluxes in three shielded integral channels: electrons >0.26, >0.4, and >1.9 MeV, and protons >6.3, >9.5, and >35 MeV, with 64 s time resolution.

Dynamics Explorer 1 SAI (Spin-Scan Auroral Imager) visible and VUV (vacuum ultraviolet) spin-scan photometric imager measuring global auroral emissions and geocoronal hydrogen, producing 36°×120° images every ~3–12 min in channels including 3914, 5577, 6300 and 3175 Å plus Ly-α 1216 Å, O I 1304/1356 Å and broad 1370–1700 Å bands

Dynamics Explorer 2 LANG (Langmuir Probe) cylindrical electrostatic probe instrument measuring ionospheric thermal plasma electron temperature, electron or ion density, and spacecraft potential with two independent swept Langmuir sensors, providing continuous in situ plasma parameters and selected high-rate volt-ampere curves at ~0.5 s resolution along low-altitude magnetosphere-ionosphere field-line traversals

Dynamics Explorer 2 WATS (Wind and Temperature Spectrometer) retarding-potential quadrupole mass spectrometer measuring in situ thermospheric neutral wind vector components, neutral kinetic temperature, and concentrations of selected neutral gases, with an ion mode for thermal ion species at altitudes where neutral densities were too low

Equator-S ICI (Ion Composition Instrument), also cited as ESIC, energetic ion composition/time-of-flight spectrometer measuring 3D distribution functions and moments of H+, He+, He2+ (He++), and O+; combines retarding-potential, toroidal energy-per-charge, and time-of-flight analysis, covering essentially 0 or ~15 eV/q to 40 keV/q, with 6 s ion moments, closely matching Cluster CIS/CODIF

Cluster-Tango/C4 CIS (Cluster Ion Spectrometry) ion spectrometer suite measuring three-dimensional ion distributions, moments, and composition; comprising HIA (Hot Ion Analyzer) for high-flux ions without mass discrimination (~5 eV/q-32 keV/q) and CODIF (Composition and Distribution Function) time-of-flight mass-per-charge analyzer resolving H+, He++, He+, and O+ from spacecraft potential/~25 eV/q to 40 keV/q.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2T EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform product giving trajectory positions, altitude, latitude, longitude, and coordinate-system locations for payload 2T of the second Antarctic BARREL balloon campaign (2013-2014), used to colocate X-ray measurements with geomagnetic and Van Allen Probes conjunctions

Cluster-Rumba EFW (Electric Field and Waves) long-wire double-probe instrument measuring spin-plane DC/AC electric fields, waveforms, spacecraft potential, plasma-density fluctuations, and Langmuir-probe density/temperature; four spherical probes on 50 m booms provide ~100 m baselines, with channels DC-10 Hz/180 Hz/4 kHz/32 kHz, AC 10 Hz-8 kHz, and frequency counter 10-200 kHz

Communication/Navigation Outage Forecasting System VEFI (Vector Electric Field Instrument) multi-sensor electric-field experiment measuring AC/DC ionospheric electric fields, plasma density structure, magnetic field, and optical lightning signatures; comprising three orthogonal 20 m tip-to-tip double-probe electric antennas, a fixed-bias Langmuir probe, a fluxgate magnetometer, and an optical lightning detector

BARREL Balloon 2Q DPU (Data Processing Unit) payload controller/platform for Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses payload 2Q of the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), acquiring data from the X-ray spectrometer (XRI), magnetometer, Global Positioning System receiver, and Engineering Data Interface for framed Iridium downlink and cutdown commanding

Equator-S PCD (Potential Control Device) active spacecraft-potential control ion emitter controlling spacecraft charging by emitting variable 6 keV indium ion beams, reducing positive spacecraft potential to a few volts so 3DA and other plasma instruments could measure low-energy particles; beam current could be fixed or feedback-controlled from the 3DA electron spectrum.

Dynamics Explorer 2 MAG-B (Magnetic Field Observations) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic fields for field-aligned current and magnetosphere-ionosphere-atmosphere coupling studies in the auroral oval and polar cap; ±6.2×10^4 nT range, 1.5 nT resolution, ±4 nT accuracy, 25 Hz bandwidth, 16 vectors s^-1 sampling

CANOPUS BARS (Bistatic Auroral Radar System) coherent VHF radar measuring high-latitude ionospheric field-aligned irregularity backscatter power and Doppler velocity/shift; a 48 MHz bistatic pair at Nipawin, Saskatchewan, and Red Lake, Ontario, using a broad transmit beam and 8 receive fan beams with range gating for 2-D auroral convection maps

MMS-4 SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) magnetometer measuring three-axis AC magnetic-field fluctuations and plasma waves from ~1 Hz to 6 kHz; one of the MMS-4 FIELDS suite sensors alongside AFG (Analog Fluxgate), DFG (Digital Fluxgate), SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument)

Dynamics Explorer 2 RPA (Retarding Potential Analyzer) retarding potential analyzer measuring ram ion drift, ion temperature, spacecraft potential, density irregularity spectra, and thermal ion composition (H+, He+, O+, N+ and molecular ions near perigee) from ion flux versus retarding-voltage sweeps (~0 to +32 V), with a wide-aperture duct sensor for total ion concentration irregularities

Equator-S EPI (Energetic Particle Instrument) solid-state energetic-particle telescope array measuring energetic electron and ion intensities and angular distributions; physically part of the Three-dimensional plasma analyzer (3DA), covering electrons at 20-226 keV and ions at 20-400 keV in 6 energy channels and 4 simultaneous angle channels, sampling ~70% of 4π per spacecraft spin

BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2F DPU (Data Processing Unit) payload controller for the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), acquiring X-ray spectrometer, magnetometer, GPS, and EDI engineering data, formatting Iridium downlink frames, and supporting cutdown command functions rather than making standalone science measurements

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2O DPU (Data Processing Unit), payload-control and data-handling platform supporting measurements in the second Antarctic balloon campaign (2013-2014), acquiring framed data from the XRI (X-ray instrument) scintillator spectrometer (~10 keV-10 MeV), magnetometer, GPS (Global Positioning System), and EDI (Engineering Data Interface); not an independent science detector.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2F XRI (X-ray instrument) NaI scintillator spectrometer measuring bremsstrahlung X-ray spectra and flux from precipitating radiation-belt electrons; payload 2F of the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), 10 keV-10 MeV response, 50 ms rates in 10-180, 180-550, 550-840, 840-1500 keV bands, plus 48-channel 4 s and 256-channel 32 s spectra from 20 keV-7 MeV

GOES-13 (2010–2017) SEM (Space Environment Monitor) suite, GOES-N series/GOES-East 2010–2017, measuring geostationary space weather: solar soft X-ray irradiance/flux with XRS (X-Ray Sensor) 0.05–0.3 and 0.1–0.8 nm bands, solar EUV flux with EUVS (Extreme Ultraviolet Sensor) ~10–126 nm, energetic electrons/protons/alpha particles with EPS (Energetic Particle Sensor) and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector), and geomagnetic/local vector magnetic field with MAG (Magnetometer)

Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) Series, F18 (2009–present) SESS/SSM-Boom (Space Environment Sensor Suite/Special Sensor Magnetometer boom) boom-mounted triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic-field fluctuations and perturbations in low-altitude polar orbit for auroral electrodynamics, field-aligned currents, ionospheric currents, and storm/substorm magnetic signatures.

GOES-6 (1983–1994) EPM (Energetic Particle Monitor) energetic particle instrument measuring geostationary energetic proton, alpha-particle, and >500 keV electron fluxes; first-generation GOES-6 unit with lower-energy detector assemblies: proton P1–P7 (0.8–500 MeV), alpha A1–A6 (4 to >400 MeV), electron (>500 keV), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector; >370 MeV protons, >640 MeV/nucleon alphas)

GOES-9 (1995–1998) SEM (Space Environment Monitor), GOES-I/M-generation space-weather suite at geostationary orbit measuring magnetic field, solar soft X-ray flux, and energetic particles, comprising MFS (Magnetic Field Sensor, ±1000 nT), XRS (X-Ray Sensor, 0.5–4 and 1–8 Å), EPS/EP8 (Energetic Particle Sensor, protons ~0.8–500 MeV; electrons >0.6, >2, >4 MeV), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector, protons >350 MeV; alphas >640 MeV/nucleon)

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2M EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual trajectory product providing payload position versus time from GPS-derived balloon ephemeris in geographic and geomagnetic coordinate systems; unit 2M of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign (2013-2014), used to locate X-ray measurements relative to radiation-belt field lines

Dawn Ephemeris (spacecraft positions) platform/trajectory data product providing Dawn spacecraft position and velocity versus time, used to locate the spacecraft relative to Earth, the Sun, Vesta, Ceres, and other solar-system bodies for context of Dawn science observations; not a particle, field, plasma, or imaging instrument

Cluster-Salsa EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) active electron-beam drift instrument measuring magnetospheric convection electric field, E×B drift velocity, magnetic-field magnitude, and ∇B drift/field-gradient effects; uses coded 0.5 and 1 keV test electron beams emitted and detected after one gyroperiod by two opposing gun-detector units on Cluster FM6 Salsa.

CSSWE (Colorado Student Space Weather Experiment) REPTile (Relativistic Electron and Proton Telescope integrated little experiment) loaded-disc collimated solid-state particle telescope measuring directional differential fluxes of radiation-belt electrons in E1 0.58-1.63 MeV and E2 1.63-3.8 MeV, and protons in P1 8-18 MeV, P2 18-30 MeV, and P3 30-40 MeV

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2Y EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product measuring time-tagged balloon trajectory positions for payload 2Y of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign (2013-2014), including latitude, longitude, altitude, and geomagnetic coordinates used to locate X-ray measurements from precipitating radiation-belt electrons

Geotail CPI (Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation) quadrispherical analyzer suite measuring 3-D electron and positive-ion velocity distributions and ion composition; comprising the HP (Hot Plasma) analyzer for electrons and ions at 1-50,000 eV/q, the SW (Solar Wind) ion analyzer at 150-7,000 eV/q, and the IC (Ion Composition) analyzer covering ~1-550 u/q at 100 eV and ~1-55 u/q at 10 keV

CANOPUS (Canadian Auroral Network for the OPEN Program Unified Study) ASI (All-Sky Imagers) ground-based optical auroral imager array measuring all-sky visible auroral luminosity, morphology, and motion over the Canadian high-latitude ionosphere, often analyzed with CANOPUS magnetometers, riometers, and meridian-scanning photometers in International Solar-Terrestrial Physics/Global Geospace Science studies

Cluster JSOC (Joint Science Operations Centre) virtual instrument measuring no physical heliospheric quantities, but providing Cluster Model Data for the Cluster-1/Rumba, Cluster-2/Salsa, Cluster-3/Samba, and Cluster-4/Tango constellation: predicted planning data, payload operation plans, spacecraft/instrument commanding context, and model/attitude/operations information used to interpret Cluster observations.

Cluster-Tango PEACE (Plasma Electron and Current Experiment) dual electrostatic electron analyzer measuring 3-D electron velocity distributions, moments, currents, spacecraft potential and pitch-angle distributions from 0.67 eV to 30 keV; comprising LEEA (Low Energy Electron Analyzer) and HEEA (High Energy Electron Analyzer).

FAST ESA (Electro-Static Analyzers) electrostatic analyzer suite measuring auroral electron and ion distribution functions, energy spectra, and pitch-angle distributions from ~3 eV to 30 keV over 360° field of view; comprising EESA (Electron Electrostatic Analyzer), IESA (Ion Electrostatic Analyzer), and high-time-resolution SESA (Stepped Electrostatic Analyzer) sensors in four stacks

Cluster-Rumba DWP (Digital Wave Processor) wave-processing and coordination instrument measuring onboard particle-count autocorrelations and supporting WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium) electric and magnetic plasma-wave observations from DC to >100 kHz; one of the five WEC experiments alongside EFW, STAFF, WHISPER, and WBD

BARREL Balloon 2N EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product recording trajectory positions for unit 2N of the second BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Antarctic campaign, 2013-2014, with time-tagged latitude, longitude, altitude, and magnetospheric coordinates used to locate its X-ray observations

CRRES MEA (Medium Electron Sensor) energetic electron spectrometer, Sensor A of the Medium Energy Electron Spectrometer, measuring temporal, spectral, and spin-resolved directional electron fluxes in the radiation belts over ~47 keV to 2.2 MeV, commonly cited as 100–2000 keV, with 17 medium-energy electron channels and a shielded background counter for proton/bremsstrahlung contamination

FAST (Fast Auroral Snapshot Explorer) EFLP (Electric Field and Langmuir Probe Experiment) electric-field and Langmuir-probe instrument measuring vector electric fields from static fields to ~20 kHz (0.1 mV/m-1 V/m), waveforms to 2 MHz, thermal plasma density (1-10^5 cm^-3), temperature, density fluctuations, antenna time delays, and interferometric wavelengths using ten boom sensors on radial and axial booms

Cluster-Tango (C4) EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) active electron-beam drift instrument measuring perpendicular electric field/convection drift, magnetic-field magnitude, and magnetic-gradient drift by emitting weak coded test-electron beams (typically 0.5 and 1 keV) from two opposed gun-detector units and detecting their one-gyration returns in the magnetosphere

Cluster-Salsa ASPOC (Active Spacecraft Potential Control) spacecraft-potential control instrument measuring spacecraft charging and regulating it with an adjustable ~6 keV indium ion beam (<50 µA), using EFW (Electric Fields and Waves) or PEACE (Plasma Electron And Current Experiment) potential estimates to improve cold-plasma distributions and electric-field measurements.

Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) Series SESS/SSI/ES-3, including DMSP F16 (2003–2020), one ES-3 (Electron Sensor-3) swept Langmuir probe/SSIES-3 (Special Sensor-Ions, Electrons, and Scintillation-3) sensor measuring in-situ ambient ionospheric electron density, electron temperature, and spacecraft potential near the ~840 km polar DMSP orbit, alongside RPA-3 (Retarding Potential Analyzer), IDM-3 (Ion Drift Meter), and SM-3 (Scintillation Meter)

Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) Series SESS/SSJ5, including DMSP F16 (2003–2020): SSJ5 (Special Sensor J/5 precipitating electron and ion electrostatic spectrometer) measuring precipitating auroral electron/ion differential number and energy flux in 19 fixed energy channels from ~30/50 eV to 30 keV; part of SESS (Space Environment Sensor Suite) alongside SSM (Special Sensor Magnetometer) and SSIES (Special Sensor Ions, Electrons, and Scintillation)

Cluster-Rumba STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) wave magnetometer measuring magnetic field fluctuations in the WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium); comprising STAFF-SC (search coil) triaxial magnetic waveform sensor (0.1-10 Hz normal, to 180 Hz high rate) and STAFF-SA (spectrum analyzer) deriving 3B+2E spectral matrices with EFW (Electric Field and Wave) data over 8 Hz-4 kHz (64 Hz-4 kHz high rate)

ELFIN A (Electron Losses and Fields Investigation) EPD (Energetic Particle Detector) solid-state particle telescope suite measuring spin-resolved pitch-angle distributions of radiation-belt electrons (~50 keV-5 MeV) and ions/protons (~250 keV-5 MeV); comprising EPD-E/EPDE electron telescope and EPD-I/EPDI ion telescope on the ELFIN-A CubeSat

Dynamics Explorer 2 VEFI (Vector Electric Field Instrument) double-probe antenna electric field instrument measuring ionospheric direct-current and low-frequency electric fields; designed for triaxial ±1 V/m fields at 16 samples/s with ~0.1 mV/m resolution and variational fields from 4-1024 Hz (~1 µV/m-10 mV/m root-mean-square), but flown with the orbit-normal antenna pair undeployed

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2L DPU (Data Processing Unit) payload controller acquiring and formatting X-ray spectrometer, magnetometer, GPS (Global Positioning System), and engineering/EDI (Engineering Data Interface) data for Iridium downlink and cutdown control; unit 2L of the second Antarctic balloon campaign, 2013-2014

Cluster-Tango (C4) STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetometer and wave spectrum analyzer measuring magnetic field fluctuations and electromagnetic wave spectral matrices; comprising STAFF-SC triaxial search-coil waveforms (0.1-10 Hz normal, 0.1-180 Hz high bit rate) and STAFF-SA auto/cross-spectra using 3 B and 2 E components from ~8 Hz to 4 kHz

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2E DPU (Data Processing Unit) flight computer for the second Antarctic campaign, 2013-2014, acquiring and framing XRI X-ray spectrometer counts, magnetometer vectors, GPS position/time, and EDI engineering housekeeping for Iridium downlink and payload command/cutdown support

DMSP Series DMSP-F18 (2009–present) SESS/SSJ5 (Space Environment Sensor Suite/Special Sensor Precipitating Electron and Ion Spectrometer 5) electrostatic spectrometer measuring precipitating auroral electron and ion differential number and energy fluxes along the spacecraft zenith/nadir look direction in fixed energy channels from ~30/50 eV to 30 keV

Cluster-Samba Ephemeris (spacecraft orbit/position) platform data product providing time-tagged C3/Samba spacecraft position in geocentric solar ecliptic (GSE), geocentric solar magnetospheric (GSM), geocentric equatorial inertial (GEI), and related coordinates for Cluster Mission science context

FAST (Fast Auroral Snapshot Explorer) Ephemeris spacecraft-position data product providing derived spacecraft location and velocity rather than detector measurements; used to tag FAST auroral particle-and-field observations with geocentric/geographic and magnetic coordinates such as altitude, latitude, longitude, magnetic local time, invariant latitude, and L shell along its polar low-Earth orbit

BARREL Balloon 2X DPU (Data Processing Unit), flight platform of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), acquiring and formatting X-ray spectrometer data, magnetometer vectors, Global Positioning System position/time, and Engineering Data Interface housekeeping for Iridium downlink and cutdown commanding

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2T MAG (Magnetometer) three-axis tilt-compensated magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector components at 1 s cadence with ~10 nT resolution using the TCM2 (Tilt Compensated Magnetometer 2) sensor, for identifying substorm activity and ultra-low-frequency (ULF) magnetic oscillations; payload 2T of the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014)

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2F MAG (Magnetometer) three-axis TCM2 tilt-compensated magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic-field variations at 1 s cadence with ~10–50 nT resolution for substorm and ULF-wave context; payload 2F of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign, 2013–2014

Cluster-Samba (SC3) WBD (Wide Band Data) wideband plasma-wave receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric/magnetic waveforms and spectra in the magnetosphere, 25 Hz-577 kHz, using selectable EFW (Electric Fields and Waves) antennas or STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetic components; Wave Experiments Consortium with EFW, STAFF, WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing Electron density by Relaxation), and DWP (Digital Wave Processing).

GOES-10 (1998–2009) GOES-K SEM (Space Environment Monitor) space-weather suite in GOES I-M series (1997–2009), measuring geostationary/magnetospheric energetic electrons and protons, solar soft X-ray flux, and magnetic field; EPS/EP8 (Energetic Particle Sensor; protons 0.8–500 MeV, electrons), HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector; protons >350 MeV, alphas >640 MeV/n), XRS (X-Ray Sensor; 0.5–4 and 1–8 Å), MFS (Magnetic Field Sensor; ±1000 nT vector field)

GOES-8 (1995–2003) GOES (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites) Ephemeris platform data product reporting spacecraft position and orbit state for time-tagged observations, identifying the GOES-I first-generation Imager/Sounder geostationary spacecraft launched in 1994 and used as GOES-East/GOES-South context rather than a science sensor

Cluster-Samba RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) energetic particle imaging spectrometer measuring suprathermal/energetic electrons (20-400 keV), ions (2 keV/nucleon-1.5 MeV/nucleon; H, He, CNO groups) and energetic neutral atoms (10-100 keV), comprising IIMS (Imaging Ion Mass Spectrometer, three SCENIC heads) and IES (Imaging Electron Spectrometer)

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2K DPU (Data Processing Unit) flight computer and telemetry controller acquiring and packetizing XRI (X-ray instrument) spectrometer counts, fluxgate magnetometer, GPS (Global Positioning System), and EDI (Engineering Data Interface) housekeeping data; payload 2K of the second Antarctic balloon campaign (2013-2014)

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2I EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product providing trajectory positions, altitude, and time-tagged payload location in multiple coordinate systems for payload 2I of the second Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), used to locate its X-ray measurements in geospace.

IMAGE EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet Imager) wide-field ultraviolet imager measuring global plasmaspheric He+ column abundance and plasmapause structure via resonantly scattered 30.4 nm emission; three 30° sensor heads form an 84° × 30° fan swept by spacecraft spin to image cold-plasma morphology and dynamics with ~0.6° angular resolution and ~10 min cadence.

Polar CAMMICE (Charge and Mass Magnetospheric Ion Composition Experiment) energetic-particle ion composition suite measuring magnetospheric ion mass, charge, energy spectra, and angular distributions from <10 keV/Q to 15 MeV/Q for H through Fe; comprising MICS (Magnetospheric Ion Composition Sensor) and HIT (Heavy Ion Telescope), used for plasma-sheet and ring-current populations

Interball-1 Ephemeris spacecraft orbit data product providing the Interball-1/Tail Probe position and velocity versus time for locating in situ plasma, magnetic-field, energetic-particle, and wave measurements in geocentric coordinates, especially high-apogee magnetotail, magnetopause, and solar-wind context intervals

Interball-1 SKA-2 (Low and Energetic Charged Particle Composition and Anisotropy) energetic-particle ion spectrometer measuring solar wind H+ and He++ fluxes, composition, and energy-angular distributions near the Sun direction with high time resolution, supporting proton/alpha anisotropy studies in the magnetospheric tail environment

Interball-1 MIF-M (Multicomponent Investigations of Fluctuations of Magnetic Fields) magnetometer measuring magnetic-field fluctuations on the Interball Tail Probe/ASPI fields-and-waves payload, using triaxial fluxgate channels for DC 0-2 Hz and AC 2-25 Hz fields plus a Z-axis search-coil channel from 1 Hz to 40 kHz and a seven-band analog filter bank.

Parker Solar Probe TDS (Time Domain Sampler) waveform receiver measuring burst electric- and magnetic-field waveforms for the FIELDS suite, one of the FIELDS processors alongside DFB (Digital Fields Board), RFS (Radio Frequency Spectrometer), MAG (fluxgate magnetometers) and SCM (search-coil magnetometer); samples five channels from electric antennas V1-V5 and one SCM axis at up to 1.92 MSa/s, ~1 MHz Nyquist

MetOp-A (2006–2021) SEM-2 (Space Environmental Monitor-2) multi-channel energetic charged-particle spectrometer measuring satellite-altitude/low-Earth-orbit auroral and radiation-belt particle fluxes and radiation-belt intensity; comprising TED (Total Energy Detector, electrons and ions in 0.05–20 keV bands), MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector, electrons/protons/ions from ~30 keV to >6.9 MeV), and a common processing unit.

Interball-2 PROMICS-3 (PROGNOZ Magnetospheric Ion Composition Spectrometer) electrostatic analyzer suite measuring 3-D ion distributions with mass separation M=1–32 from 4 eV to 70 keV and electron distributions from 12 eV to 35 keV; comprising MEPS (magnetospheric electron plasma spectrometer) and TRICS (three-dimensional ion composition spectrometer) sensors

International GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) Service (IGS) GPS (Global Positioning System) receiver ground-based radio waveform receiver measuring dual-frequency L-band GNSS code, carrier phase, Doppler, and signal strength observables (notably GPS L1 1575.42 MHz and L2 1227.60 MHz) for precise orbits, clocks, station positions, and ionospheric total electron content.

MMS-4 FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) magnetometer measuring DC magnetic-field vectors for reconnection and current structures; part of the FIELDS suite alongside EDP (Electric Double Probe), SCM (Search-Coil Magnetometer), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), with redundant AFG (Analog Fluxgate) and DFG (Digital Fluxgate) sensors, typically used at 128 vectors/s burst cadence

Interball-2 DOK-2A (Electron and Proton Anisotropy) energetic particle telescope measuring auroral/magnetospheric electron and proton fluxes, spectra, and pitch-angle anisotropy; four silicon telescopes 1e/2e for electrons (20-420 keV) and 1p/2p for ions/protons (20-850 keV), with a fixed antisolar pair and a mechanically scanning pair for 3-D distributions over each spin

Pioneer Venus Orbiter ORPA (Orbiter Retarding Potential Analyzer) Langmuir-probe retarding potential analyzer measuring Venus ionospheric electron density and temperature, major ion concentrations and temperatures, ion drift velocities, and ambient photoelectron energy distributions with multigrid cup sensors operated in electron, ion, or photoelectron modes

MMS-3 (Magnetospheric Multiscale) EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) electron-beam drift instrument in the FIELDS suite measuring DC electric field, E×B convection velocity, and magnetic field from ~1 keV test-electron gyromotion/time of flight; sibling FIELDS sensors are AFG (Analog Fluxgate), DFG (Digital Fluxgate), SCM (Search-Coil Magnetometer), and EDP (Electric Double Probe: SDP spin-plane, ADP axial).

MAVEN (Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution) SEP (Solar Energetic Particle) solid-state telescope instrument measuring energetic electron and proton fluxes, spectra, and angular distributions at Mars; comprising SEP1 and SEP2 orthogonal dual-ended silicon telescopes providing four look directions, with proton channels 25 keV-6 MeV, electron channels 25 keV-1 MeV, flux dynamic range ~20-10^7 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1, and 2-32 s cadences

MMS-1 DSP (Digital Signal Processor) FIELDS wave-processing instrument measuring electric- and magnetic-field fluctuations by digitizing SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), and SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) signals for waveform, spectral, burst, and Solitary Wave Detector products; one FIELDS suite element alongside FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument)

Parker Solar Probe V5 (Voltage Probe 5) antenna measuring single-ended electric potential and plasma/radio wave voltage in the FIELDS suite; a boom-mounted umbra voltage sensor complementing the sunlit V1-V4 electric-field antennas, MAGi/MAGo fluxgate magnetometers, SCM search-coil magnetometer, RFS radio-frequency spectrometer, and DFB digital fields board

Parker Solar Probe V2 (Voltage Probe 2) antenna measuring spacecraft-to-plasma potential, electric-field components, plasma waves, and radio-frequency voltage signals for the FIELDS suite; one of five voltage probes alongside V1, V3, V4 sunlit electric antennas and the boom-mounted V5 sensor, used with MAG and SCM magnetic-field sensors

MMS-1 (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 1) ADP (Axial Double Probe) double-sphere electric-field instrument measuring the spin-axis electric-field component for 3-D DC to 100 kHz electric fields; part of the FIELDS suite alongside SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), DFG (digital fluxgate magnetometer), AFG (analog fluxgate magnetometer), SCM (search-coil magnetometer), and EDI (electron drift instrument)

MMS-2 FIELDS/DSP (Digital Signal Processor) waveform/spectral processor measuring AC electric-field and search-coil magnetic-field waves (~1 Hz-6 kHz), a MMS-2 FIELDS suite component with SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer) and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument); produces waveforms, spectra, spectral matrices and SWD (Solitary Wave Detector) triggers

Parker Solar Probe FIELDS (Fields Experiment) V4 (Voltage Probe 4) voltage-probe antenna measuring electric potential, DC/low-frequency electric fields, and radio/plasma waves; one of the five FIELDS electric antennas alongside V1, V2, V3, and V5, with V4 one of the four sunlit heat-shield-mounted probes used for double-probe and capacitive wave measurements

MMS-2 EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) electron-beam drift instrument measuring DC convection electric field, E×B drift, and magnetic-field geometry using coded ~1 keV electron beams; one of the MMS-2 FIELDS suite sensors alongside AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer), SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), and ADP (Axial Double Probe)

MMS-3 DSP (Digital Signal Processor) FIELDS suite wave processor measuring electric- and magnetic-field waveforms and spectra from the SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), and SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), including onboard filtering, spectral products, burst wave capture, and Solitary Wave Detector event selection alongside AFG, DFG, EDI, and CIDP.

MMS-4 ADP (Axial Double Probe) double-sphere electric-field instrument measuring the spin-axis electric-field component from DC to 100 kHz; part of the MMS-4 FIELDS suite alongside SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), AFG/DFG (Analog/Digital Fluxgate Magnetometers), and SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), enabling full 3-D electric fields when combined with SDP.

Parker Solar Probe SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) search-coil magnetometer measuring three-component AC magnetic-field fluctuations and plasma waves from 10 Hz-50 kHz plus one LF/MF component from 1 kHz-1 MHz; a FIELDS suite sensor alongside the MAG fluxgate magnetometers, RFS radio receivers, TDS waveform sampler, DFB spectral processor, and electric-field antennas

MMS-3 (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 3) FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) vector magnetometer measuring quasi-static magnetic field strength and direction; a FIELDS suite sensor alongside SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), EDP (Electric Double Probe: SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe) and ADP (Axial Double Probe)), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), combining AFG (Analog Fluxgate) and DFG (Digital Fluxgate) sensors
