SESAME (Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic Measurements) RIO (relative ionospheric opacity meter) riometer measuring ionospheric absorption of cosmic radio noise in dB; reports north, east, south, and west look directions transformed to an L-shell-aligned coordinate system at 1 s cadence with ~0.1 dB sensitivity

STEREO-A IMPACT/HET (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients/High Energy Telescope) particle telescope measuring solar energetic protons (~13-100 MeV), helium (~14-100 MeV/nucleon) and electrons (~0.7-6 MeV); IMPACT sibling sensors are MAG (magnetometer), SWEA (solar wind electron analyzer), STE (suprathermal electron), SEPT (solar electron proton telescope), SIT (suprathermal ion telescope) and LET (low energy telescope)

STEREO-A (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory Ahead) STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope), an IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) energetic-particle telescope measuring ~2-20 keV suprathermal electrons in two oppositely directed Parker-spiral views, alongside MAG, SWEA, SEPT, SIT, LET, and HET for solar-wind, flare, shock, and interplanetary CME studies

Fort St. John Geophysical Observatory FSJ (Fort St. John) ground magnetometer measuring geomagnetic field strength and vector components/variations at the British Columbia, Canada observatory, used for magnetic storms, substorms, auroral electrojet activity, Pc pulsations, and ground magnetic response to solar-wind and magnetospheric disturbances

Mekrijarvi Geophysical Observatory MEK (Mekrijarvi) fluxgate magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field vector variations, typically reported as X/Y/Z or H/D/Z components, for ULF pulsations, magnetic bays, substorms, and auroral electrojet disturbances; the MEK station is commonly used with Finnish/IMAGE ground magnetometer data.

THEMIS-D MOM (On-Board Moments) plasma moment data product deriving spin-resolution ion and electron moments from ESA (Electrostatic Analyzer) and SST (Solid State Telescope) distributions, including density, particle and energy flux, velocity, pressure, temperature, and six-component symmetric momentum-flux tensor in DSL, GSE, GSM, and MFA coordinates

THEMIS-E ESA (Electrostatic Analyzer) dual top-hat electrostatic analyzer pair measuring thermal plasma electron and ion 3-D distribution functions, fluxes, moments, density, bulk velocity, and temperature over ~3 eV–30 keV with near-4π/360° spin-resolved coverage; comprising the electron ESA (eESA) and ion ESA (iESA) sensors on probe E/TH-E.

Loysburg Geophysical Observatory LOYS (Loysburg) magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic observatory instrument measuring three-component magnetic-field variations and absolute/vector geomagnetic field at the Loysburg station, reported as H/D/Z or north/east/down components for geomagnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, and ionospheric current studies

Baranov Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer ground-based geomagnetic field magnetometer measuring local vector variations of Earth’s magnetic field (H, D, Z or X, Y, Z components) and total field at the high-Arctic Cape Baranova/Severnaya Zemlya station, used for magnetospheric disturbance, auroral electrojet, Pc pulsation, and geomagnetic storm studies

Radiation Belt Storm Probes B (RBSP-B) RPS (Relativistic Proton Spectrometer) energetic-particle telescope measuring trapped inner Van Allen belt protons from 50 MeV to 2 GeV, with silicon-stack channels to ~400 MeV and Cherenkov response above ~400 MeV for radiation-belt flux, dose, displacement-damage, and model-validation studies.

Student Nitric Oxide Explorer (SNOE) UVS (Ultraviolet Spectrometer) ultraviolet limb spectrometer measuring thermospheric nitric oxide (NO) density from NO gamma bands, with two 3.7 nm-bandpass channels centered on the (1,0) band at 215 nm and the (0,1) band at 237 nm, providing limb altitude profiles with ~3.5 km vertical resolution and 27 ms integrations.

STEREO-A PLASTIC (PLAsma and SupraThermal Ion Composition) time-of-flight electrostatic analyzer measuring solar-wind and suprathermal ion composition, M and M/q, energy spectra, and arrival direction over ~0.3-80 keV/q; key cited channels are the SWS Small Channel for H+ and He++, SWS Main Channel for heavy ions (C, O, Mg, Si, Fe), and Wide Angle Partition for pickup/local ions including He+ <40 keV/q

Cape Dorset Geophysical Observatory CDRT (Cape Dorset) ground magnetometer measuring geomagnetic field variations in vector components (typically X/Y/Z or H/D/Z) for high-latitude ionospheric current, auroral electrojet, substorm, magnetic-storm, and ULF pulsation studies at the Cape Dorset, Nunavut station

STEREO-A IMPACT (In situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) particle-and-field suite measuring the interplanetary magnetic field, solar-wind electrons, and suprathermal/energetic particles; comprising MAG (Magnetometer), SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer, <1 eV to several keV electrons), STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope, ~2-20 keV electrons), SEPT (Solar Electron Proton Telescope, 20-400 keV electrons and 20 keV-7 MeV protons), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope, He-Fe ions at 30 keV/n-2 MeV/n), LET (Low Energy Telescope, 1.5-30 MeV/n ions), and HET (High Energy Telescope, ions to ~100 MeV/n and electrons to ~5 MeV)

Athabasca Geophysical Observatory ATHA (Athabasca) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field variations at the Athabasca, Alberta auroral-zone station, providing north/east/vertical or H/D/Z magnetic components for studies of ULF pulsations, substorms, auroral electrojets, and solar-wind–magnetosphere coupling

ST5-224 Ephemeris (Space Technology 5 spacecraft 224 ephemeris) platform position data product specifying the ST5-224 observatory trajectory and location in geocentric coordinate systems, used to contextualize ST5 magnetometer observations by orbit position, altitude, latitude/longitude, magnetic coordinates, and local time rather than measuring a plasma or field quantity

SAMPEX (Solar Anomalous and Magnetospheric Particle Explorer) PET (Proton-Electron Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring magnetospheric and solar energetic electrons from 1-30 MeV, including >0.4 MeV high-rate precipitating-electron counts, protons and helium from 18-85 MeV/nucleon (trackable to several hundred MeV/nucleon), and heavier nuclei from 54-195 MeV/nucleon

Fort Nelson Geophysical Observatory FTN (Fort Nelson) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations and magnetic perturbations from ionospheric currents, substorms, magnetic storms, and ultra-low-frequency pulsations for auroral-zone/mid-latitude geospace studies

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) BFE (Brorfelde) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and magnetic field variations at the Brorfelde geomagnetic observatory in Denmark, cited by its IAGA station identifier BFE for studies of geomagnetic disturbances, pulsations, and magnetic indices

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) FSM (Fort Smith) ground magnetometer measuring geomagnetic field vector components and local magnetic perturbations at the Fort Smith station, IAGA identifier FSM, for studies of magnetospheric current systems, substorms, geomagnetic storms, and ionospheric electrodynamics

THEMIS-A (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms) Ephemeris platform/status data product providing probe A/THA spacecraft position and velocity, geocentric solar ecliptic and geocentric solar magnetospheric coordinates, orbital location, attitude, spin-phase context, and ancillary status for interpreting THEMIS-A field and particle measurements

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) IVA Ivalo Magnetometer, ground-based geomagnetic field instrument measuring vector magnetic-field components and variations at the Ivalo, Finland observatory station with IAGA code IVA, used for auroral-zone magnetic disturbance, substorm, pulsation, and geomagnetic-index studies

THEMIS-A MOM (On Board Moments) onboard plasma moments product measuring ion and electron density, number/energy flux, bulk velocity, pressure, temperature, and six-component momentum flux tensor from combined ESA (Electrostatic Analyzer) and SST (Solid State Telescope) particle data, corrected with EFI (Electric Field Instrument) spacecraft potential, with spin-resolution outputs in DSL (Despun Sun–L-vector), GSE, GSM, and MFA coordinates

Clyde River Geophysical Observatory CRVR (Clyde River) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field variations at the Clyde River, Nunavut station, providing vector magnetic perturbations typically cited as CRVR/Clyde River data for auroral, ionospheric current, ULF wave, and geomagnetic storm studies.

Bay Mills Geophysical Observatory BMLS (Bay Mills) ground magnetometer measuring the local geomagnetic field vector and its time variations at the Bay Mills, Michigan station, providing observatory magnetic components for studies of geomagnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, ionospheric currents, and magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling

Hot Springs Geophysical Observatory HOTS (Hot Springs) Magnetometer ground-based geomagnetic observatory magnetometer measuring Earth’s magnetic-field variations at the Hot Springs station, reported as vector components such as H, D, Z or X, Y, Z and often total intensity F, for studies of geomagnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, and solar-wind–magnetosphere coupling

STEREO-A (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory Ahead) IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients)/SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer) top-hat electrostatic analyzer measuring solar wind core, halo, and strahl electron distribution functions and pitch-angle distributions from <1 eV to several keV with near-4π angular coverage, alongside IMPACT MAG, STE, SEPT, SIT, LET, and HET

Nuuk Geophysical Observatory GDH magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic observatory magnetometer at Nuuk/Godthåb, Greenland, measuring vector geomagnetic field components and magnetic field variations (H/D/Z or X/Y/Z, with total field F) for high-latitude ionospheric current, substorm, auroral electrojet, and space-weather studies.

Kilpisjarvi Geophysical Observatory KIL (Kilpisjärvi) ground-based fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field variations (H/D/Z or north/east/down components) at the Finnish auroral-zone station, widely used for auroral electrojet, substorm, ULF pulsation, Pi/Pc, and geomagnetic disturbance studies, including IMAGE network analyses

Donna Geophysical Observatory magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic observatory magnetometer at Donna, Texas, measuring local magnetic-field strength and vector variations in standard observatory components such as H/D/Z or X/Y/Z for studies of geomagnetic disturbances, magnetic storms, ionospheric currents, and solar-wind–magnetosphere coupling.

Kuujjuaq Geophysical Observatory KUUJ (Kuujjuaq) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and temporal magnetic variations at the Kuujjuaq, Québec high-latitude observatory, used for auroral-zone geomagnetic activity, magnetic pulsations, substorms, and magnetosphere-ionosphere current studies

Linares Geophysical Observatory LRES (Linares Geophysical Observatory) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector components and temporal variations, reporting standard observatory quantities such as H, D, Z or X, Y, Z and total field F for magnetic disturbances, pulsations, storms, and substorm signatures at the Linares station

RBSP-B (Radiation Belt Storm Probe B, Van Allen Probe B) EFW (Electric Field and Waves) fields-and-waves suite measuring three-component quasi-static electric fields, spacecraft potential/cold plasma density, and electric and magnetic wave spectra/waveforms in the inner magnetosphere, using spin-plane and spin-axis double-probe sensors: continuous fields to 12 Hz, spectra ~1 Hz-12 kHz, burst waveforms to >500 kHz.

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) HAN Hankasalmi magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic observatory/station instrument in Finland measuring vector magnetic-field components and variations for auroral-zone current systems, magnetic storms, substorms, and ULF pulsations under the IAGA station identifier HAN

THEMIS-D EFI (Electric Field Instrument) double-sphere electric-field instrument measuring three-component ambient electric fields, waveform fields from DC to 4 kHz and AC-coupled differential fields ~10 Hz-8 kHz, onboard spectra and 100-400 kHz integrated power, plus individual V1-V6 and differential E12/E34/E56 probe potentials/spacecraft floating potential using four spin-plane wire booms and two axial booms

Tasiilaq Geophysical Observatory AMK (Ammassalik) ground magnetometer measuring geomagnetic field variations at the East Greenland auroral-zone station, reporting vector components such as H, D, Z or X, Y, Z and total field F for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, ionospheric currents, and high-latitude geomagnetic activity.

THEMIS-A (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms) SST (Solid State Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring superthermal electron and ion directional flux/energy-flux spectrograms with two sensor heads sweeping most of the sky; primary ranges are ions 30-300 keV and electrons 30-100 keV, with extended capability ~20 keV-6 MeV ions and ~25 keV-1 MeV electrons.

Nain Geophysical Observatory Nain Magnetometer ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations (H, D, Z or X, Y, Z) and magnetic disturbances at Nain, Labrador, supporting auroral-zone studies of substorms, geomagnetic storms, ULF waves, and ionospheric/magnetospheric current systems.

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) FSP (Fort Simpson) magnetometer ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector components and temporal variations at Fort Simpson, Northwest Territories, Canada, used for magnetic storms, substorms, auroral electrojet currents, and ULF geomagnetic pulsations

Americus Geophysical Observatory AMER (Americus) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength and vector variations for geomagnetic indices and disturbance studies, reported as station AMER with north/east/vertical or horizontal/declination/vertical components and scalar total field used in magnetospheric and ionospheric current analyses

Homer Geophysical Observatory MAG (Magnetometer) ground-based geomagnetic field instrument measuring local vector magnetic field variations and perturbations in the H/D/Z or X/Y/Z components, used for auroral electrojet, substorm, geomagnetic storm, ULF wave, and ionospheric current studies at the Homer, Alaska observatory

STEREO-A SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope) time-of-flight ion mass spectrometer in IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) measuring elemental composition and spectra of suprathermal He-Fe ions from 30 keV/n to 2 MeV/n; energetic-particle sibling to SEPT (Solar Electron and Proton Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope), and HET (High Energy Telescope)

STEREO-B SEPT (Solar Electron and Proton Telescope) particle telescope of IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) measuring electrons (~30-400 keV) and protons/ions (~60 keV-7 MeV); sibling energetic-particle sensors include STE (Suprathermal Electron), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope) and HET (High Energy Telescope), with SEPT-E and SEPT-N/S magnet/foil views along/against the Parker spiral and north/south of the ecliptic

SESAME VELOX (Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic Measurements VLF/ELF Logger Experiment) 10-channel very-low-frequency/extremely-low-frequency waveform receiver measuring magnetospheric radio waves from 0.5-30 kHz, used for whistler-mode propagation, wave-particle interactions, wave-induced precipitation, and plasma structure studies with typical 1 min recordings every 15 min

THEMIS-D (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms) ESA (Electrostatic Analyzer) thermal plasma instrument measuring full 3-D ion and electron distributions, fluxes, and moments (density, velocity, temperature) from ~3 eV to 30 keV; comprising separate ion ESA and electron ESA sensors, complemented on THEMIS-D by the SST energetic particle telescopes

Danmarkshavn Geophysical Observatory DMH (Danmarkshavn) magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and time variations at the high-latitude East Greenland station, providing ground magnetic data for auroral electrojet, polar-cap convection, field-aligned current, substorm, and geomagnetic storm studies

Kapuskasing Geophysical Observatory KAPU (Kapuskasing) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field strength and temporal variations at the Kapuskasing, Ontario station, used for local magnetic perturbations, substorm/auroral-zone activity, and magnetospheric current-system studies in north-east-down or H-D-Z components

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) BBG Barentsburg Magnetometer ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field strength and variations at the Barentsburg, Svalbard station, cited by IAGA observatory code BBG for high-latitude magnetic disturbance and auroral-zone studies

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) LUC (Lucky Lake) Magnetometer ground-based magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector components and magnetic field variations at the Lucky Lake station, IAGA identifier LUC, commonly used for geomagnetic indices, substorm, magnetic-storm, and ionospheric current studies.

STEREO-B SWAVES (STEREO/WAVES) radio and plasma wave instrument measuring solar Type II/III radio bursts, source direction/size, in-situ Langmuir/plasma waves and electric-field waveforms from ~2.5 kHz to 16 MHz; comprising the HFR (High Frequency Receiver), LFR (Low Frequency Receiver), FFR (Fixed Frequency Receiver) and TDS (Time Domain Sampler) using three orthogonal 6 m monopoles

Goose Bay Geophysical Observatory GBAY (Goose Bay) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at the Goose Bay, Labrador station, including H-D-Z or north/east/vertical magnetic perturbations used to study auroral currents, magnetic storms, substorms, and ultra-low-frequency pulsations.

Akulivik Geophysical Observatory AKUL (Akulivik) ground-based fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at the Akulivik, Quebec station, used for auroral-zone magnetic perturbations, substorm current systems, geomagnetic indices, and ultra-low-frequency pulsations in conjunction with Canadian high-latitude magnetometer arrays

Kuujjuarapik Geophysical Observatory KJPK (Kuujjuarapik) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength and vector variations at the Quebec auroral-zone observatory, typically reported as H, D, Z or X, Y, Z components for magnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, and ionospheric current studies

Daneborg Geophysical Observatory DNB (Daneborg) ground magnetometer measuring geomagnetic field vector components and temporal variations at the Daneborg station in northeast Greenland, supporting studies of auroral-zone ionospheric currents, substorms, magnetic pulsations, and geomagnetic storms in Greenland magnetometer data sets

Chibougamau Geophysical Observatory CHBG (Chibougamau) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength, vector components, and time variations; data are typically cited by station code CHBG with H, D, Z or X, Y, Z component channels for geomagnetic storms, substorms, magnetic bays, and pulsations at the Quebec observatory

STEREO-B IMPACT/MAG (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory-B In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector interplanetary magnetic-field strength/direction (up to ~8 vectors/s, auto-ranging); one suite sensor alongside SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer), STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope), SEPT (Solar Electron and Proton Telescope), and SIT/LET/HET (Suprathermal Ion, Low Energy and High Energy Telescopes)

instruments.mission_name: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2, RENU 2, Sounding Rocket Payload
instruments.description: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 UVPMT (Ultraviolet Photomultiplier Tube) photomultiplier-tube photometer measuring far-ultraviolet airglow with peak response at atomic oxygen 130.4 nm, flown on the RENU 2 sounding-rocket payload into the dayside cusp from Andøya on 13 Dec 2015 to diagnose neutral upwelling/thermospheric response

STEREO-B PLASTIC (Plasma and SupraThermal Ion Composition) ion composition mass spectrometer measuring solar-wind and suprathermal ion energy spectra, direction, mass and M/q from ~0.3–80 keV/q; includes SWS Small Channel for H+ and He++, SWS Main Channel for heavy solar-wind ions C, O, Mg, Si and Fe, and the Wide Angle Partition for H+, He++, He+ and pickup He+ (<40 keV/q)

THEMIS-C FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) magnetometer on the Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms C spacecraft measuring vector DC/background magnetic field and low-frequency fluctuations to 64 Hz with ~0.01 nT precision; science products include FGL low-resolution, FGH high-resolution/burst and FGS spin-fit data in despun spacecraft, geocentric solar ecliptic and geocentric solar magnetospheric coordinates

Rosetta Ephemeris spacecraft trajectory and position data product reporting the Rosetta orbiter location and velocity versus time, used to determine heliocentric, cometocentric, and planetary context for measurements near comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko and during interplanetary cruise/flybys

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) BLC (Baker Lake) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field components and time variations at the Baker Lake, Nunavut station, providing IAGA-code BLC magnetic observatory data for ionospheric, magnetospheric, and space-weather studies

SESAME AIS (Advanced Ionospheric Sounder) high-frequency dynasonde/radar sounder measuring ionospheric echo time of flight, amplitude, and phase versus frequency and time over 0.1–30 MHz, with ~1–3° phase accuracy; used to diagnose electron-density structure, auroral arcs, and localized energetic-particle precipitation

McGrath Geophysical Observatory MCGR (McGrath) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field variations and magnetic perturbations at the McGrath, Alaska station, used in heliophysics studies of auroral-zone currents, geomagnetic storms, substorms, and ground magnetic indices or station time series

Inukjuak Geophysical Observatory INUK (Inukjuak) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and nT-level magnetic perturbations at the Inukjuak, Québec observatory, used for auroral-zone current systems, substorms, geomagnetic storms, pulsations, and regional magnetic indices/arrays.

Ekati Geophysical Observatory magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic field instrument measuring local vector magnetic field variations at the Ekati/EKT auroral-zone station, used for H/D/Z or north/east/down perturbations, substorm current systems, geomagnetic pulsations, and magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling studies.

Jackvik Geophysical Observatory magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic field instrument at the Jäckvik/Jackvik station (often cited by station code JCK) measuring vector magnetic field components and time variations/perturbations used for auroral electrojet, substorm, geomagnetic storm, and ULF wave studies

Eagle Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer ground-based magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at the Eagle station, providing local magnetic perturbations in H/D/Z or X/Y/Z components for studies of auroral electrojets, substorms, geomagnetic storms, and magnetosphere-ionosphere current systems

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) INK (Inuvik) magnetometer, a ground geomagnetic observatory instrument at Inuvik, Northwest Territories, Canada, measuring local Earth magnetic field components and temporal variations for studies of geomagnetic disturbances, auroral electrojets, substorms, and solar-wind/magnetosphere coupling

THEMIS-C EFI (Electric Field Instrument) double-sphere electric-field experiment measuring the three-component ambient vector electric field, waveforms and spectra from DC to 4 kHz (AC-coupled differentials ~10 Hz-8 kHz), and 100-400 kHz band power; uses six probes on four spin-plane wire booms and two axial booms, providing V1-V6/Emn potentials, spin-fit E, spacecraft potential and high-time-resolution density estimates

instruments.mission_name: NASA Stennis Space Center Geophysical Observatory
instruments.description: NASA Stennis Space Center BSL (Bay St. Louis) Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer ground magnetometer measuring time-varying geomagnetic field components and magnetic disturbances at the Stennis, Mississippi observatory for space-weather, ionospheric-current, and geomagnetic-storm studies.

Bjorn Magnetometer magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength and vector variations at the Bjorn geophysical observatory, used for ground-based monitoring of auroral-zone magnetic perturbations, ionospheric current systems, geomagnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, and magnetic indices; cited as the Bjorn or Bjørnøya ground magnetometer.

Lethbridge Geophysical Observatory LETH (Lethbridge) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector variations, typically reported as north/east/vertical or H/D/Z components, at the Lethbridge, Alberta station for studies of geomagnetic disturbances, auroral electrojet currents, substorms, magnetic storms, and ULF pulsations.

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) LRV Leirvogur Magnetometer ground-based geomagnetic observatory magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field variations and vector components (X/Y/Z or H/D/Z) and total field F at the Leirvogur station in Iceland, commonly cited by IAGA code LRV.

Masi Geophysical Observatory MAS (Masi) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic-field variations and magnetic pulsations in north/east/down or X/Y/Z components at the auroral-zone Masi station, used for IMAGE/SuperMAG-style studies of ionospheric currents, substorms, and geomagnetic disturbances

THEMIS-D (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms probe D) FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) magnetometer measuring the vector background magnetic field and low-frequency fluctuations to 64 Hz in near-Earth space and solar wind, with FGS spin-fit (~3 s), FGL low-resolution (4 Hz) and FGH burst/high-resolution (128 Hz) science data products

Glyndon Geophysical Observatory GLYN (Glyndon) ground-based magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations (H/D/Z or north/east/vertical perturbations) at the Glyndon station for studies of auroral electrojets, ULF pulsations, magnetic storms, and substorm current systems

STEREO-B Ephemeris (Solar TErrestrial RElations Observatory Behind spacecraft position) platform ephemeris data product measuring spacecraft position, velocity, heliocentric distance, heliographic/HEE/HEEQ longitude-latitude, and Earth-Sun-spacecraft separation in common heliophysics coordinate systems for the STEREO-B context.

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) BRW (Barrow) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength and vector components/declination-inclination at the Barrow/Utqiaġvik, Alaska observatory, used for auroral-zone magnetic disturbances, substorms, magnetic pulsations, and geomagnetic storms

Paamiut Geophysical Observatory FHB (Frederikshåb/Paamiut) ground-based magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and variations at Paamiut, southwest Greenland, for studies of auroral/subauroral magnetic disturbances, ionospheric currents, magnetic storms, substorms, and ULF pulsations.

RBSP-A EFW (Electric Field and Waves) electric-field and plasma-wave suite measuring three-dimensional electric fields from quasi-static to >500 kHz, spin-plane and spin-axis convection fields to 12 Hz, spacecraft potential for cold plasma density (~0.1-100 cm-3), and electric/magnetic wave spectra, cross spectra, and burst waveforms around 1 Hz-12 kHz.

Kullorsuaq Geophysical Observatory KUV (Kullorsuaq) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic-field components and time variations at the Kullorsuaq, northwest Greenland station, used for auroral-zone magnetic perturbations, geomagnetic pulsations, substorm signatures, and ionospheric current/electrojet studies.

Dededo Geophysical Observatory DED magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field variations at the Guam low-latitude observatory, providing vector components H, D, Z or X, Y, Z and total field F for studies of magnetic storms, Sq/equatorial electrojet variability, ULF pulsations, and solar-wind–magnetosphere coupling

STEREO-B SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer) particle detector measuring solar-wind core, halo, and strahl electron distribution functions and pitch-angle spectra from <1 eV to ~3 keV; one of the IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients) suite sensors alongside MAG, STE, SEPT, SIT, LET, and HET
