instruments.description: Bennington BENN (Bennington Geophysical Observatory) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field strength and temporal variations at the Bennington, Vermont station, used for geomagnetic activity, magnetic pulsations, substorm, storm-time disturbance, and regional ionospheric-current studies

Carson City Geophysical Observatory CCNV (Carson City, Nevada) magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field vector components and local magnetic perturbations, providing station time series of north/east/vertical or H/D/Z variations used in magnetospheric current, substorm, and geomagnetic-storm studies

ST5-094 Ephemeris (Space Technology 5 spacecraft 094 ephemeris) platform/trajectory data product giving spacecraft position and orbit state vectors in heliophysics coordinate systems such as geocentric, GSE, GSM, and SM; unit 094 of the 2006 ST5 three-microsatellite magnetospheric technology-demonstration constellation.

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) DOB Dombas magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic field instrument at the Dombås, Norway station measuring local magnetic field components and variations for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, ionospheric currents, and regional geomagnetic activity.

THEMIS-E SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) triaxial induction magnetometer measuring AC magnetic-field fluctuations and wave spectra in the magnetosphere from 0.1 Hz to 4 kHz, extending to 8 kHz in wave burst; data products include fbk filter-bank bands (4-2 kHz to 4-2 Hz), scf fast survey, scp particle burst, scw wave burst, and ffp/ffw FFT spectra

Solar Orbiter Ephemeris virtual platform product providing spacecraft position and velocity, trajectory, heliocentric distance, heliographic latitude/longitude, and observing geometry for the Solar Orbiter spacecraft; used to contextualize in situ and remote-sensing measurements rather than a physical sensor.

Derby Geophysical Observatory Derby Magnetometer ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field variations and absolute field at Derby, Western Australia, providing vector components commonly reported as H/D/Z or X/Y/Z and total field F for geomagnetic disturbance, pulsation, substorm, and ionospheric current studies

Kevo Geophysical Observatory KEV (International Monitor for Auroral Geomagnetic Effects station code KEV) ground-based fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations in nT, reported as X, Y, Z or H, D, Z components for auroral electrojet, substorm, and ULF pulsation studies in northern Finland

Kodiak Geophysical Observatory KOD (Kodiak) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field variations at the Kodiak, Alaska auroral-zone station, providing H, D, Z or X, Y, Z magnetic-component time series used for magnetic storms, substorms, ionospheric currents, Pc/ULF pulsations, and high-latitude geospace disturbance studies

THEMIS-B THEMIS (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms) Ephemeris platform status product giving spacecraft position, velocity, time tags and ancillary probe state for the B observatory, used to locate in-situ fields and particle measurements in geocentric, solar-magnetospheric, and lunar-orbit contexts

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) CMO (College Magnetic Observatory) ground magnetometer at College/Fairbanks, Alaska measuring the geomagnetic field vector and variations, reported as X/Y/Z or H/D/Z components and total intensity F, for auroral-zone magnetic disturbances, substorms, storms, and geomagnetic indices

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) IQA (Iqaluit) magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field vector components and time variations at the high-latitude Canadian Arctic station; station code IQA data are used for auroral electrojet, substorm, storm, ULF pulsation, and magnetosphere-ionosphere current studies, with components commonly cited as X/Y/Z or H/D/Z

THEMIS-D THEMIS (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms) Ephemeris platform data product reporting spacecraft position, velocity, geocentric/orbit coordinates, attitude/spin state, timing, and probe status for the THEMIS-D/P4 spacecraft, used to contextualize fields and particles observations rather than as a science sensor

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) LOZ (Lovozero) magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic observatory instrument measuring local Earth magnetic field components and temporal variations at the Lovozero, Russia station, used for geomagnetic disturbances, pulsations, auroral electrojet, and magnetosphere-ionosphere current studies.

THEMIS-B ESA (Electrostatic Analyzer) thermal plasma spectrometer measuring full 3-D electron and ion distribution functions, fluxes, density, velocity, and temperature over ~3 eV–30 keV with separate electron ESA and ion ESA sensors on the THEMIS-B spacecraft in the THEMIS constellation

SESAME (Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic Measurements) FPI (Fabry-Perot Interferometer) ground-based optical interferometer measuring Doppler shifts and line widths of atomic oxygen airglow/auroral emissions, especially O I 630.0 nm, to derive thermospheric neutral winds and temperatures while scanning cardinal look directions at ~30° elevation.

Harris Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer ground-based magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic-field vector variations (H/D/Z or north/east/vertical components) and magnetic pulsations, storms, and substorm signatures for studies of ionospheric and magnetospheric current systems at the Harris station.

THEMIS-C (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms C) Ephemeris/Probe Status platform data product providing spacecraft position, velocity, orbit context, attitude/spin and health/status quantities for the THC probe, used to locate THEMIS-C measurements relative to Earth’s magnetosphere and solar-wind coordinates.

RBSP-A (Radiation Belt Storm Probe A) Ephemeris spacecraft ephemeris/platform data product measuring the Van Allen Probe A spacecraft position and orbit context in geocentric coordinate systems, including position vectors commonly used for radiation-belt studies such as GEO, GSE, GSM, SM, and magnetic coordinates for conjunction and mapping analyses

Laurel Geophysical Observatory LGO (Laurel Geophysical Observatory) ground magnetometer measuring the local geomagnetic field vector and time variations at Laurel, Maryland, providing observatory magnetic components such as H/D/Z or X/Y/Z and total-field disturbances for studies of geomagnetic activity, substorms, storms, and ionospheric current systems

SAMPEX (Solar, Anomalous, and Magnetospheric Particle Explorer) MAST (Mass Spectrometer Telescope) solid-state energetic-particle telescope measuring isotopic composition and energy spectra of energetic nuclei from lithium through nickel (Z=3-28) at ~10 to several hundred MeV/nucleon with ~0.2 amu mass resolution, complementing LICA (Low Energy Ion Composition Analyzer), HILT (Heavy Ion Large Telescope), and PET (Proton/Electron Telescope)

STEREO-A (Solar TErrestrial RElations Observatory Ahead) IMPACT/MAG (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients Magnetometer) tri-axial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the DC interplanetary magnetic-field vector on the boom, with auto-ranging sensitivity for low solar-wind fields up to near-Earth commissioning fields; one IMPACT sensor alongside SWEA, STE, SEPT, SIT, LET, and HET.

THEMIS-E MOM (On Board Moments) onboard plasma-moment processor measuring ion and electron density, number/energy flux, velocity, pressure, temperature, and six-component momentum-flux tensor from combined ESA (Electrostatic Analyzer) and SST (Solid State Telescope) data, with EFI (Electric Field Instrument) spacecraft-potential corrections and outputs in DSL, GSE, GSM, and MFA coordinates

THEMIS-B MOM (On Board Moments) processing system deriving spin-resolution electron and ion plasma moments from ESA (Electrostatic Analyzer) and SST (Solid State Telescope) data, measuring number density, number and energy flux, velocity, pressure, temperature, and six-component momentum-flux tensor in DSL, GSE, GSM, and MFA coordinates, with spacecraft-potential correction from EFI

RBSP-B Ephemeris (Radiation Belt Storm Probe B spacecraft positions) platform/ancillary data product measuring the Van Allen Probe B spacecraft location and state vector for orbit context, reported in geocentric coordinate systems such as geographic/geocentric, Geocentric Solar Ecliptic, Geocentric Solar Magnetospheric, and Solar Magnetic coordinates

La Ronge Geophysical Observatory LRG (La Ronge) ground-based fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations and ULF pulsations, magnetic bays, and substorm/auroral electrojet perturbations in northward, eastward, and vertical components at the La Ronge, Saskatchewan observatory station

STEREO-A IMPACT/SEPT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients/Solar Electron Proton Telescope) particle telescope measuring 20–400 keV electrons and 20 keV–7 MeV protons; one IMPACT sensor alongside MAG (magnetometer), SWEA (solar wind electron analyzer), STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope) and HET (High Energy Telescope), with SEPT-E and SEPT-N/S look directions for anisotropy

SESAME (Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic MEasurements) MAG (Magnetometer) fluxgate magnetometer measuring the terrestrial magnetic-field H, D, and Z components for coordinated Antarctic geospace studies, with 1 s sampling cadence and approximately 1 nT field resolution.

THEMIS-B EFI (Electric Field Instrument) double-probe electric-field instrument measuring the 3-D ambient electric field, probe potentials, spacecraft floating potential and high-time-resolution density proxy; six spherical sensors on four spin-plane wire booms and two axial booms provide DC fields, waveforms to 4 kHz, AC-coupled differentials ~10 Hz-8 kHz, spectra, and 100-400 kHz integrated wave power

Attu Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer ground-based geomagnetic magnetometer measuring local vector variations of Earth’s magnetic field at Attu, Alaska, typically reported as H/D/Z or north/east/vertical components for studies of auroral electrojets, magnetic storms, substorms, and ULF/Pc pulsations in the high-latitude ionosphere-magnetosphere system

Coral Harbour Geophysical Observatory CHBR (Coral Harbour) ground magnetometer measuring high-latitude geomagnetic field components and temporal variations at Coral Harbour, Nunavut, Canada, for auroral-zone studies of magnetic storms, substorms, ULF pulsations, and ionospheric current systems

THEMIS-A (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms probe A) FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the DC vector magnetic field and low-frequency fluctuations to 64 Hz with ~0.01 nT sensitivity; data products include FGL low-rate survey, FGH 128 sps burst, and FGS spin-fit magnetic field in DSL, GSE, and GSM coordinates

instruments.mission_name: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2, RENU 2, Sounding Rocket Payload
instruments.description: RENU 2 (Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2) IG2 (Ion Gauge 2) ion-gauge package measuring neutral particle density, primarily atomic oxygen number density, along the NASA dayside-cusp sounding-rocket trajectory from Andøya on 13 Dec 2015; comprising six Aerospace-provided Anelva ion gauges on the RENU 2 payload

STEREO-B IMPACT/HET (Solar TErrestrial RElations Observatory-B In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients/High Energy Telescope) particle telescope measuring solar energetic protons and helium nuclei from ~13 to >100 MeV/nucleon and electrons to ~5–6 MeV, one IMPACT sensor alongside LET (Low Energy Telescope), SIT, SEPT, STE, SWEA, and MAG.

THEMIS-B FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) fluxgate magnetometer measuring the DC vector/background magnetic field and low-frequency magnetic fluctuations to 64 Hz with ~0.01 nT precision; science products include FGL low-resolution 4 Hz, FGH high-resolution 128 Hz burst, FGS 3 s spin-fit, and FGE engineering data in DSL, GSE, and GSM coordinates

RBSP-B EMFISIS (Electric and Magnetic Field Instrument Suite and Integrated Science) waveform receiver and magnetometer suite measuring ambient magnetic fields, plasma waves, and electron density; comprising MAG (fluxgate magnetometer, quasi-static vector B to 15 Hz), WFR (Waveform Receiver, 10 Hz-12 kHz electric and magnetic spectra/spectral matrices), and HFR (High Frequency Receiver, 10-400 kHz electric spectra including upper-hybrid resonance)

THEMIS-C SST (Solid State Telescope) energetic particle instrument measuring directional superthermal electron and ion fluxes, spectra, and pitch-angle distributions; two SST heads scan nearly the full sky, with common ground-calculated electron/ion flux spectrogram channels ~30-300 keV and sensor capability to ~25 keV-1 MeV electrons and ~20 keV-6 MeV ions

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) Fredericksburg/FRD magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field variations at the Fredericksburg, Virginia observatory; citable station code FRD, reporting standard observatory components such as X/Y/Z, H/D/Z and scalar F for magnetospheric, ionospheric, and space-weather studies

STEREO-A SWAVES (Solar TErrestrial RElations Observatory/WAVES) radio and plasma wave instrument measuring solar type II/III radio bursts, source direction/size, and in situ electric-field plasma waves/waveforms from ~2.5 kHz to 16 MHz; comprising HFR (High Frequency Receiver), LFR (Low Frequency Receiver), FFR (Fixed Frequency Receiver, 10-40 kHz) and TDS (Time Domain Sampler), using three orthogonal 6 m monopole antennas

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) MEA (Meanook) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength and variations at the Meanook observatory station in Alberta, Canada, providing vector components commonly reported as H-D-Z or X-Y-Z and total field F for geomagnetic disturbance and current-system studies

STEREO-A (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory Ahead) Ephemeris platform/ancillary data product reporting the spacecraft trajectory and position vectors in multiple heliocentric, geocentric, and mission coordinate systems, used to locate STEREO-A for contextual analysis of in-situ fields/particles and remote solar observations

Bettles Geophysical Observatory BETT (Bettles, Alaska) ground-based magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength and vector variations, reported as standard horizontal, declination/east-west, and vertical components for auroral-zone magnetic disturbances, substorms, pulsations, and geomagnetic activity studies

STEREO-A LET (Low Energy Telescope) particle detector measuring solar energetic H-Ni ions at ~3-30 MeV/n, including 3He and trans-iron nuclei Z=30-83, with composition, spectra, angular distributions, and timing; one of four IMPACT SEP sensors alongside SEPT, SIT, and HET.

STEREO-B SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope) time-of-flight ion mass spectrometer in IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients) measuring He-Fe suprathermal ion composition and spectra from ~30 keV/n to 2 MeV/n; energetic-particle sensor alongside SEPT, LET, and HET, with a 17°×44° field of view for solar energetic particle, CME-shock, and CIR ions

Hornepayne Geophysical Observatory HRP (Hornepayne) ground-based magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field variations at the Hornepayne, Ontario station, used for local magnetic perturbations, ULF pulsations, auroral electrojet and magnetospheric-ionospheric current signatures in geospace studies.

SAMPEX HILT (Heavy Ion Large Telescope) energetic-particle telescope measuring charge, energy, mass, and species-resolved fluxes of heavy ions and cosmic rays; one of four SAMPEX particle instruments alongside LICA, MAST, and PET, covering ~8-310 MeV/nucleon overall, including He 3.9-90, C 7.2-160, O 8.3-310, Ne 9.1-250, and Fe 11-90 MeV/nucleon

THEMIS-A SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) triaxial induction-coil magnetometer measuring AC magnetic-field fluctuations and wave magnetic spectra from ~0.1 Hz to 4 kHz, extending to ~8 kHz in wave-burst data; a THEMIS fields/waves sensor used with EFI, FGM, and DFB products, including SCM waveform, filter-bank, and FFT spectral channels.

Gakona Geophysical Observatory GAK (Gakona) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at the Alaska HAARP/Gakona site, used for auroral-zone magnetic perturbations, substorm signatures, geomagnetic pulsations, ULF wave activity, and ionospheric current response studies.

Igloolik Geophysical Observatory IGLO (Igloolik) magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field variations at the high-latitude Canadian Arctic station, providing vector magnetic components for studies of auroral electrojets, ULF pulsations, substorms, magnetic storms, and magnetosphere-ionosphere current systems at Igloolik, Nunavut

RBSP-B RBSPICE (Radiation Belt Storm Probes Ion Composition Experiment) energetic-particle spectrometer measuring ring-current and radiation-belt ion composition, spectra, pressure and pitch-angle distributions; its Puck time-of-flight/solid-state sensor resolves H+, He+ and O+ ions from ~40 keV to ~1 MeV and electrons from ~25 keV to ~1 MeV.

THEMIS (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms)-Ground Chibougamau ASI (All-Sky Imager) ground optical imager measuring panchromatic auroral luminosity, morphology, and motion over Chibougamau, Québec, Canada, with ~170° all-sky field of view, 256×256 images, typical 3 s cadence, and kilometer-scale auroral resolution for substorm studies

THEMIS-E Ephemeris (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms probe E ephemeris) platform status product measuring spacecraft position, velocity, attitude/spin state, and orbit geometry for the THEMIS-E spacecraft, used to locate its plasma, field, and particle observations within the five-probe THEMIS constellation

Muono Geophysical Observatory magnetometer, commonly cited as the Muonio station code MUO, ground fluxgate magnetometer measuring geomagnetic field variations in north/east/down or H/D/Z components for auroral electrojet, substorm, magnetic pulsation, and space-weather studies in the high-latitude Fennoscandian sector

THEMIS-E (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms probe E) FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) magnetometer measuring the DC/vector background magnetic field and low-frequency fluctuations to 64 Hz with ~0.01 nT sensitivity; data products include FGS spin-fit 3 s, FGL low-resolution 1/4 s, FGH high-resolution/burst 1/128 s, and FGE engineering 1/8 s in DSL, GSE, and GSM coordinates

THEMIS-D SST (Solid State Telescope) energetic particle instrument measuring spin-resolved superthermal electron and ion fluxes and spectra in the magnetosphere; two solid-state telescope heads provide opposing electron and ion look directions, with primary calibrated ranges of ~30-100 keV electrons and ~30-300 keV ions, extending to ~25-1000 keV electrons and ~20-6000 keV ions

RBSP-B ECT (Energetic Particle, Composition, and Thermal Plasma Suite) energetic particle suite measuring inner-magnetospheric electrons and ions, composition, spectra, pitch-angle distributions, and radiation-belt dynamics from ~1 eV to tens of MeV; comprising HOPE (Helium Oxygen Proton Electron), MagEIS (Magnetic Electron Ion Spectrometer), and REPT (Relativistic Electron Proton Telescope)

Gjoa Haven Geophysical Observatory GJOA (Gjoa Haven Geophysical Observatory) ground-based magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations and absolute/vector magnetic perturbations for auroral-zone, ionospheric-current, substorm, and magnetospheric activity studies at Gjoa Haven, Nunavut, Canada

THEMIS-B SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) triaxial search-coil magnetometer in the THEMIS (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms) fields suite alongside FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) and EFI (Electric Field Instrument), measuring 3-D wave magnetic-field fluctuations from 0.1 Hz to 4 kHz, up to 8 kHz, with fbk filter-bank, scf/scp/scw waveform and ffp/ffw spectral products

IAGA AMU (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) Anchorage ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector variations at the AMU station, used for geomagnetic activity, magnetic-storm, substorm, and pulsation studies via the IAGA observatory identifier AMU.

RBSP-A EMFISIS (Electric and Magnetic Field Instrument Suite and Integrated Science) waveform and field suite measuring DC magnetic fields, plasma waves, wave spectra, wave normals, Poynting flux, and upper-hybrid density; comprising MAG (tri-axial fluxgate magnetometer, DC-15 Hz) and WAVES with search-coil magnetic fields 10 Hz-12 kHz, spin-plane electric fields 10 Hz-12 kHz, and single-channel electric fields 10-400 kHz.

STEREO-B (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory Behind) IMPACT (In situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) particles-and-fields suite measuring interplanetary magnetic-field vectors, solar-wind/suprathermal electrons, and energetic particle fluxes/composition; comprising MAG (magnetometer), SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer, <1 eV-several keV electrons), STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope, ~2-20 keV electrons), SEPT (Solar Electron and Proton Telescope, 20-400 keV electrons and 20 keV-7 MeV protons), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope, He-Fe ions 30 keV/n-2 MeV/n), LET (Low Energy Telescope, 1.5-13 MeV/n hydrogen/helium and 2-30 MeV/n heavy ions), and HET (High Energy Telescope, hydrogen/helium to ~100 MeV/n and electrons to ~5 MeV).

Lyford Geophysical Observatory magnetometer ground-based vector magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field strength and variations at the Lyford, New Hampshire station; used for local magnetic disturbances, magnetic storms, substorm bays, and ultra-low-frequency pulsations in H/D/Z or X/Y/Z components

Dead Horse Geophysical Observatory DED (Dead Horse) magnetometer, a high-latitude Alaska ground geomagnetic observatory instrument measuring vector geomagnetic field components and field variations for auroral, magnetospheric, and ionospheric current studies, commonly cited by station code DED/Deadhorse alongside other observatory magnetometers.

Nord Geophysical Observatory NOR (Nordkapp) fluxgate magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic-field vector components and temporal variations, typically reported as H/D/Z or X/Y/Z magnetic components for auroral-zone magnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, and ionospheric current studies

Ulysses SWICS (Solar Wind Ion Composition Spectrometer) solar-wind ion composition/time-of-flight mass spectrometer measuring elemental and ionic charge-state composition, temperatures and bulk speeds of ions H through Fe, plus pickup and suprathermal ions, over 110 eV/q-66.7 keV/q and solar-wind speeds 145-1350 km/s.

Wind SWICS (Solar Wind Ion Composition Spectrometer) solar-wind ion composition spectrometer measuring ion energy, mass, mass-per-charge, charge states, elemental and isotopic composition from ~0.5-30 keV/e; one of the three SMS (Solar Wind and Suprathermal Ion Composition) suite sensors alongside MASS (Mass Time-of-Flight Spectrometer) and STICS (Suprathermal Ion Composition Spectrometer)

Upernavik Geophysical Observatory UPN (Upernavik) magnetometer measuring ground-based geomagnetic field strength and vector variations at the Upernavik, Greenland auroral-zone station, used for magnetic perturbations, substorm/electrojet activity, and high-latitude ionospheric current studies.

Pevek Geophysical Observatory PBK (IAGA station code) magnetometer instrument measuring the ground geomagnetic vector field and temporal variations at the Arctic Pevek station, reporting standard observatory components (H, D, Z or X, Y, Z) for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, auroral-zone currents, and ultra-low-frequency pulsations.

Ulysses SWOOPS (Solar Wind Observations Over the Poles of the Sun) electrostatic analyzer plasma instrument measuring solar wind ion and electron velocity distributions, density, speed, temperature, and proton/alpha bulk parameters; comprising an electron analyzer (1-900 eV) and a solar wind ion analyzer (257 eV-35 keV/q) for heliospheric and Jovian plasma studies

TIMED SABER (Sounding of the Atmosphere using Broadband Emission Radiometry) infrared limb-sounding radiometer measuring terrestrial horizon emissions in 10 bands from 1.27-16.9 µm to retrieve temperature and vertical profiles of ozone, water vapor, carbon dioxide, nitric oxide, hydroxyl/oxygen airglow and radiative cooling from the surface to ~180 km.

Tartu Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer ground-based magnetometer measuring the local geomagnetic field and its temporal variations at the Tartu observatory in Estonia, providing magnetic observatory data for geomagnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, and solar-terrestrial disturbance studies

Solund Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer ground-based vector magnetometer measuring the three-component geomagnetic field and field perturbations, commonly reported as X/Y/Z or H/D/Z, at the Solund, Norway station for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, Pc pulsations, and ionospheric or auroral current systems

Tiksi Geophysical Observatory TIK (Tiksi) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength and vector variations at the Arctic Siberian station, reported as H/D/Z or X/Y/Z components and used for auroral electrojet, Pc pulsation, substorm, and geomagnetic storm studies in high-latitude magnetometer networks

Trapper Creek Geophysical Observatory TRAP magnetometer ground-based fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at Trapper Creek, Alaska, used for ULF pulsations, magnetic bays, auroral electrojet and substorm signatures, and regional magnetospheric-ionospheric current systems

Wind EPACT (Energetic Particle Acceleration, Composition and Transport) energetic-particle suite measuring suprathermal/energetic ions/electrons, solar energetic particles, anomalous/galactic cosmic rays, protons, He, and heavy-ion elemental/isotopic composition (~20 keV/n to ~500 MeV/n; Z to U) for acceleration/composition/transport studies; comprising STEP (Suprathermal Energetic Particle Telescope), LEMT (Low-Energy Matrix Telescope), APE (Alpha Proton Electron), and IT (Isotope Telescope)

TWINS 1 LAD (Lyman-alpha Detector) ultraviolet photometric imager measuring resonantly scattered H Lyman-alpha emission at 121.6 nm from neutral hydrogen in the terrestrial exosphere/geocorona; two independent sensors on the rotating actuator view ±40° from the spin axis with 4° FWHM fields of view, providing 360° azimuth coverage at 60 s cadence

Ny-Ålesund NYA (Ny-Ålesund) Magnetometer ground-based observatory magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field strength and variations at the high-Arctic Svalbard station, used for polar-cap and auroral magnetic perturbations, ionospheric current systems, substorms, and space-weather studies

IAGA NRD (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy Nord) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and temporal magnetic variations at the Nord high-latitude observatory in Greenland, used for auroral-zone/ polar-cap magnetic disturbance, geomagnetic index, and space-weather studies

IAGA NUR (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy Nurmijärvi Observatory) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector variations and absolute field at station code NUR in southern Finland, reported in standard observatory components such as X/Y/Z or H/D/Z/F for geomagnetic-storm, substorm, and pulsation studies

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) Ottawa Magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic observatory magnetometer at station identifier OTT, measuring vector geomagnetic field components and temporal magnetic variations for magnetic storm, substorm, pulsation, and secular-variation studies at Ottawa, Canada.

Narsarsuaq Geophysical Observatory NRSQ (Narsarsuaq) ground magnetometer measuring the local geomagnetic field vector and temporal variations at the Greenland observatory; papers cite NRSQ/Narsarsuaq magnetometer H, D, Z or X, Y, Z components for auroral electrojet, magnetic pulsation, substorm, and geomagnetic storm studies

Colville National Forest Geophysical Observatory NEW (Newport) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field variations for space-weather and magnetospheric studies, reporting observatory vector components (H/D/Z or X/Y/Z) and total intensity used in geomagnetic indices, storm, substorm, and ULF wave analyses

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) SIT (Sitka, Alaska) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and local magnetic disturbances at the Sitka observatory, commonly cited as the Sitka or SIT station magnetometer in auroral, substorm, and geomagnetic-index studies

Voyager 2 LECP (Low-Energy Charged Particles) energetic particle instrument measuring directional electrons (~10 keV to >11 MeV) and ions/protons/heavy nuclei (~15 keV to ≥150 MeV; composition Z=1–26 over ~0.05–30 MeV) in interplanetary and planetary environments, comprising the LEPT (Low-Energy Particle Telescope) and LEMPA (Low-Energy Magnetospheric Particle Analyzer) scanning through eight 45° sectors

Sept Iles Geophysical Observatory SEPT (Sept-Îles) magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field vector components and temporal variations at the Sept-Îles, Quebec station, used for magnetic storms, substorms, ULF pulsations, and high-latitude current-system studies with reported H/D/Z or X/Y/Z field components and total-field context

Ittoqqortoormiit Geophysical Observatory SCO (Scoresbysund) magnetometer ground geomagnetic observatory instrument measuring high-latitude magnetic-field variations and absolute/vector components of Earth’s field, commonly cited as the SCO Greenland station for auroral electrojet, polar-cap, Pc/ULF pulsation, and geomagnetic storm studies

Ulysses Ephemeris spacecraft trajectory/position platform data product providing the Ulysses spacecraft location and motion for heliophysics context, including heliocentric distance, heliographic latitude and longitude, and position/velocity vectors used to place plasma, field, energetic-particle, and radio measurements along the out-of-ecliptic solar polar orbit

Voyager 2 PWS (Plasma Wave System) waveform and 16-channel step-frequency receiver measuring electric-field plasma waves, electron plasma frequency/density, and wave-particle activity in planetary magnetospheres and the heliosphere from 10 Hz to 56 kHz, using the shared 10-m electric antennas of the planetary radio astronomy investigation

Shawano Geophysical Observatory SWNO (Shawano) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field variations at the Shawano, Wisconsin geophysical observatory, providing H/D/Z or X/Y/Z components in nT for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, Sq variation, Pc pulsations, and regional geomagnetic activity

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) POK (Poker Flat) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field variations and vector H, D, Z or X, Y, Z components at the Poker Flat Research Range station in Alaska; used for auroral-zone magnetic perturbations, substorms, ULF pulsations, and ionospheric current studies.

Soroya Geophysical Observatory MAG (magnetometer) ground-based fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at the high-latitude Sørøya/Soroya station in northern Norway, commonly cited as SOR, for auroral electrojet, substorm, geomagnetic-pulsation, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling studies.

The Pas Magnetometer ground-based geomagnetic observatory magnetometer measuring local variations of the terrestrial magnetic field at The Pas, Manitoba, Canada, reported as vector components (H/D/Z or X/Y/Z) for studies of substorms, magnetic bays, pulsations, and ionospheric-magnetospheric current systems

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) TUC (Tucson) Magnetometer ground geomagnetic observatory magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector components and temporal variations at the Tucson station, reported under the IAGA station identifier TUC for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, and secular field changes

Radisson Geophysical Observatory RADI (Radisson) ground-based magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector variations in north/east/vertical components, used in heliophysics papers for auroral electrojet, substorm, magnetic pulsation, and geomagnetic-activity studies over northern Québec

San Antonio Geophysical Observatory SATX (San Antonio, Texas) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field components and temporal variations at the SATX station, used for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, ULF pulsations, Sq/diurnal variation, and regional geomagnetic disturbance signatures.

TWINS-2 ENA (Energetic Neutral Atom) imager measuring charge-exchange neutral atom images of magnetospheric ion populations at ~1–100 keV; the second TWINS (Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers) flight unit, with paired wide-angle ENA sensor heads and a companion Lyman-alpha detector for geocoronal neutral hydrogen correction, identical to TWINS-1

Voyager LECP (Low-Energy Charged Particles) energetic-particle instrument measuring electrons, protons, alpha particles, and heavy ions in planetary magnetospheres and the heliosphere; comprising LEPT (Low-Energy Particle Telescope) and LEMPA (Low-Energy Magnetospheric Particle Analyzer), with 8-sector 360° scans and coverage of ~10 keV to >11 MeV electrons, ~15 keV to ≥150 MeV ions, and Z=3-26 nuclei (~0.05-30 MeV/nucleon)

WDC (World Data Center) San Juan Fluxgate Magnetometer ground-based magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and temporal variations at the San Juan geomagnetic observatory in Puerto Rico (station code SJG), providing observatory magnetic field data used for geomagnetic storms, substorms, Sq variation, and ULF pulsation studies.

PENGUIn-2 PG2 (Polar Experiment Network for Geospace Upper-atmosphere Investigations) geophysical observatory fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations and ULF pulsations at the PG2 Antarctic autonomous station for auroral electrodynamics, substorms, magnetospheric currents, and space-weather studies

Purcell Geophysical Observatory PCEL (Purcell) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field variations and vector magnetic perturbations for studies of geomagnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, and magnetosphere-ionosphere current systems at the Purcell observatory station

Val-d'Or Geophysical Observatory VLDR (Val-d'Or) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field strength and variations at the Val-d'Or, Québec station, including north/east/vertical or horizontal-intensity/declination components used to study magnetic storms, substorms, auroral electrojets, and geospace current systems

Voyager 2 MAG (Magnetic Fields Investigation) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer instrument measuring vector magnetic fields in the solar wind and the magnetospheres of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune; uses two low-field and two high-field triaxial fluxgate sensors spanning ~0.01 nT to 2×10^-3 T with ~0.1 nT interplanetary-field accuracy

Voyager 1/Voyager 2 PLS (Plasma Science) Faraday-cup plasma spectrometer measuring solar-wind and planetary-magnetospheric ion/electron distributions, bulk speed, density, temperature and pressure; comprising three coaxial Earth-pointing ion cups A, B and C and a side-looking cup D, with stepped E/q scans from ~10 eV/q to 6 keV/q and side-cup electrons ~5 eV-1 keV

TWINS-2 (Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers 2) LAD (Lyman-alpha Detector) ultraviolet photometer/imager measuring 121.6 nm hydrogen Lyman-alpha emission from neutral geocoronal H, using two independent narrowband sensors pointed ±40° from the actuator spin axis with ~4° fields of view, 360° azimuthal scan coverage, and 60 s cadence

Priddis Geophysical Observatory ROTH (Rothney Astrophysical Observatory) magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic field instrument at the Priddis/Calgary-area observatory measuring local vector magnetic-field variations and ULF pulsations in north/east/vertical or H/D/Z components for magnetospheric current and auroral-substorm studies

TWINS 1 (Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers) spacecraft ephemeris/position platform data providing the location of the TWINS-1 hosted payload in its high-inclination Molniya orbit, used to determine viewing geometry and context for TWINS ENA imaging and Lyman-alpha observations; distinct from TWINS-2 positions.

Puvirnituq Geophysical Observatory PUVR (Puvirnituq) Magnetometer ground-based fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations, local magnetic disturbances, auroral electrojet signatures, and ultra-low-frequency pulsations at the Puvirnituq, Nunavik, Quebec high-latitude station

Ulysses KET (Kiel Electron Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring high-energy electrons (~3-200 MeV) and protons and helium nuclei (~3-2100 MeV/nucleon) with dE/dx-E and Cherenkov particle identification; one of the COSPIN (Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation) suite sensors alongside HET (High Energy Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope), ATs (Anisotropy Telescopes), and HFT (High Flux Telescope)

Park Site Geophysical Observatory PKS (Park Site) magnetometer measuring ground-based geomagnetic field variations and vector components (X/Y/Z or H/D/Z, with total field where available) for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, ULF/Pc pulsations, ionospheric currents, and solar-wind–magnetosphere coupling

Remus Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer ground-based magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field variations and three-component magnetic perturbations associated with ionospheric currents, geomagnetic storms, substorms, and ultralow-frequency pulsations for space-weather and magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling studies

Ulysses HFT (High Flux Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring high-flux solar energetic particles, especially ~0.3-7 MeV protons and ~0.4-4 MeV/nucleon helium; a small-aperture COSPIN (Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation) suite sensor alongside HET (High Energy Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope), KET (Kiel Electron Telescope), and AT (Anisotropy Telescope).

Wind WAVES (Plasma and Radio Waves) waveform receiver and radio/plasma wave investigation measuring electric and magnetic field waves and solar radio emissions from sub-Hz to ~14 MHz; comprising RAD1, RAD2, TNR (Thermal Noise Receiver), TDS (Time Domain Sampler), FFT/waveform and fast-envelope channels fed by spin-plane/axial electric antennas and a triaxial search coil

Pine Ridge Geophysical Observatory PINE (Pine Ridge) ground-based magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at the PINE station, supporting studies of magnetospheric-ionospheric current systems, magnetic storms, substorms, magnetic bays, and Pc/ULF pulsations in the North American geomagnetic network

Schefferville Geophysical Observatory SCHF (Schefferville) ground fluxgate magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector variations (H/D/Z or X/Y/Z components) at the Schefferville, Québec high-latitude station for auroral electrojet, substorm, Pc/ULF pulsation, and magnetic-storm studies

Toolik Lake Geophysical Observatory TOOL (Toolik Lake) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at the Toolik Lake, Alaska station, used for auroral-zone magnetic disturbances, substorm signatures, field-line resonances, ULF pulsations, and geomagnetic indices/perturbations in the H/D/Z or north/east/vertical components

IAGA VIC (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy Victoria) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic-field vector components and temporal variations at Victoria observatory, IAGA station code VIC, including X/Y/Z or H/D/Z/F geomagnetic variations used for storms, substorms, Sq currents, and ULF pulsations

Saint-Felicien Geophysical Observatory STFL (Saint-Felicien) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector variations, typically reported as northward, eastward, and vertical magnetic components for studies of ULF waves, magnetic storms, substorms, and ionospheric/magnetospheric current systems over Quebec/North America

PENGUIn-1 Magnetometer, a PENGUIn (Polar Experiment Network for Geospace Upper-atmosphere Investigations) PG1 geophysical observatory fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component ground geomagnetic field variations for Antarctic ULF waves, magnetic pulsations, substorm signatures, and ionospheric/magnetospheric current systems.

PENGUIn-0 PG0 (Polar Experiment Network for Geospace Upper-atmosphere Investigations 0) Magnetometer ground-based vector magnetometer measuring geomagnetic field perturbations and pulsations at the Antarctic PG0 geophysical observatory for studies of ionospheric currents, magnetospheric ULF waves, substorms, and polar-cap electrodynamics.

TIMED GUVI (Global Ultraviolet Imager) far-ultraviolet cross-track scanning imaging spectrograph measuring thermosphere-ionosphere airglow and auroral emissions from 115-180 nm, with bands at H I 121.6 nm, O I 130.4 nm, O I 135.6 nm, and N2 Lyman-Birge-Hopfield 140-150 and 165-180 nm, deriving neutral composition, temperature, auroral electron energy/flux, and nightside F-region electron density

Ulysses AT (Anisotropy Telescopes) energetic particle telescope measuring ~0.7–7 MeV/n proton and helium intensities and three-dimensional anisotropies; one of the COSPIN (Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation) suite sensors alongside HET (High Energy Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope), KET (Kiel Electron Telescope), and HFT (High Flux Telescope)

Wind 3DP (Three-Dimensional Plasma and Energetic Particle) particle spectrometer suite measuring 3D electron and ion distributions, moments, pitch-angle distributions, and suprathermal/energetic particles from ~10 eV to ~5 MeV; comprising EESA-L/EESA-H (Electron Electrostatic Analyzer low/high), PESA-L/PESA-H (Proton Electrostatic Analyzer low/high), and SST Foil/Open (Solid State Telescope) sensors

Pangnirtung Geophysical Observatory PANG (Pangnirtung) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field variations (X/Y/Z or H/D/Z components) at the high-latitude Nunavut station for auroral electrojet, polar-cap current, ULF pulsation, substorm, and magnetic-storm studies

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) RIT (Rankin Inlet) magnetometer, a ground geomagnetic station instrument at Rankin Inlet, Nunavut, measuring three-component terrestrial magnetic field variations for auroral-zone magnetic disturbance, substorm, ionospheric current, and geomagnetic index studies

IAGA STJ (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy St. John's) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength, vector components, and magnetic perturbations at the St. John's observatory station in Newfoundland and Labrador; cited as the STJ or St. John's Magnetometer station data record.

Vize Island Geophysical Observatory VIZ (Vize Island) ground-based magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and temporal variations at the Arctic polar-cap observatory, providing local magnetic disturbance records for ionospheric current, auroral, substorm, and space-weather studies

IAGA TRO (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy Tromsø) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector components and temporal variations at the Tromsø, Norway observatory, IAGA station code TRO, used in heliophysics studies of auroral-zone disturbances, electrojet currents, substorms, and magnetic pulsations.

TWINS-2 (Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers) Ephemeris platform position product measuring spacecraft location, velocity, and orbit geometry versus time for the second TWINS spacecraft, used to geolocate energetic neutral atom images and provide viewing/context coordinates rather than particle or field measurements.

Voyager 2 PLS (Plasma Spectrometer) Faraday-cup plasma instrument measuring solar-wind and planetary-magnetospheric ion/electron distributions, bulk velocity, density, temperature and pressure; uses four modulated-grid Faraday cups—three earthward-facing ion cups and one side-looking electron cup—with sequential energy scans and electron coverage ~5 eV-1 keV

Ukiah Geophysical Observatory UKI magnetometer ground-based geomagnetic observatory instrument measuring variations of the terrestrial magnetic field at Ukiah, California, reporting vector components (H/D/Z or X/Y/Z) and total field F for geomagnetic storms, substorms, ULF pulsations, and magnetic-activity indices.

Prince George Geophysical Observatory PGEO (Prince George Geophysical Observatory) fluxgate magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field vector components and variations (H, D, Z/XYZ) for ULF pulsations, magnetic bays, substorms, and geomagnetic-storm disturbances; cited as the Prince George or PGEO magnetometer

Roemoe Magnetometer ground-based geomagnetic magnetometer measuring the local terrestrial magnetic field and its temporal variations at the Roemoe/Rømø geophysical observatory, providing observatory magnetic components for ionospheric, magnetospheric, geomagnetic storm, substorm, and ground magnetic disturbance studies

TIMED SEE (Solar EUV Experiment) spectrometer/photometer suite measuring full-disk solar vacuum ultraviolet, extreme ultraviolet, and soft X-ray irradiance from ~0.1–200 nm; comprising the EGS (EUV Grating Spectrograph, ~25–200 nm at ~0.4 nm resolution) and XPS (XUV Photometer System, ~0.1–34 nm in broad bands) sensors

Voyager 1 Ephemeris spacecraft trajectory and position data product providing time-tagged Voyager 1 location, range, and velocity coordinates for heliospheric context, used to relate plasma, fields, energetic-particle, and radio measurements to spacecraft position along the outbound trajectory through the outer heliosphere and interstellar medium

Ranua Geophysical Observatory RAN (Ranua station) ground fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field and field variations (typically geographic X north, Y east, Z down or H/D/Z) for auroral electrojet, substorm, ULF pulsation, and magnetic-storm studies; part of the IMAGE (International Monitor for Auroral Geomagnetic Effects) magnetometer chain in northern Finland

Red Deer Geophysical Observatory REDR (Red Deer) ground magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field components and field variations at the Red Deer, Alberta observatory, used in heliophysics papers for magnetic storms, substorms, auroral electrojet activity, ULF pulsations, and regional geomagnetic disturbance context.

Uummannaq Geophysical Observatory UMQ (Uummannaq) ground magnetometer measuring geomagnetic field components and temporal variations at the Greenland Uummannaq station, providing local magnetic perturbations for auroral-zone current systems, substorms, magnetic storms, Pc pulsations, and high-latitude ionospheric electrodynamics studies

Repulse Bay Geophysical Observatory RBAY (Repulse Bay) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength and vector variations at the Repulse Bay/Naujaat, Nunavut high-latitude station, reported as standard H, D, Z or X, Y, Z components for studies of auroral electrojets, magnetic bays, substorms, Pc pulsations, and geomagnetic storms

Summit Geophysical Observatory Summit Magnetometer ground-based fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations, ULF pulsations, and auroral/ionospheric current perturbations at Summit Station, Greenland; commonly cited as the Summit or SUM magnetometer with H/D/Z or X/Y/Z magnetic field components

PENGUIn-5 PG5 (Polar Experiment Network for Geospace Upper-atmosphere Investigations) ground fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at the Antarctic PG5 geophysical observatory, providing local H/D/Z or X/Y/Z perturbations for ULF wave, substorm, auroral electrojet and magnetosphere-ionosphere current studies

Wallops Island Geophysical Observatory WLPS (Wallops Island) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field strength, vector components, and temporal magnetic variations at the Wallops Island, Virginia station for studies of ionospheric currents, geomagnetic disturbances, substorms, and space-weather magnetic perturbations

Salluit Geophysical Observatory SALU (Salluit) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations at the high-latitude Salluit, Nunavik, Quebec station; used for auroral-zone magnetic perturbations, magnetic local time structure, ULF pulsations, substorms, and geomagnetic-storm indices/validation.

Ulysses magnetic field investigation (HED/VHM/FGM), combining a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer (FGM) and a vector helium magnetometer (VHM) to measure interplanetary magnetic field strength and direction in the inner heliosphere, including over the Sun's poles at high solar latitudes

Voyager 1/2 PWS (Plasma Wave System) waveform and spectrum receiver measuring electric-field plasma waves, Langmuir waves, whistlers, and radio-frequency wave activity in planetary magnetospheres and the solar wind; includes a 16-channel step-frequency spectrum analyzer and low-frequency waveform receiver covering 10 Hz-56 kHz, deriving electron density from plasma-wave emissions via shared 10-m electric antennas

Ulysses EPAC (Energetic Particle Composition) energetic-particle telescope experiment measuring composition, spectra, angular distributions, and anisotropies of interplanetary ions and electrons; four spin-scanned telescopes resolve H, He, and heavy nuclei to Fe over ~0.5-1.5 MeV protons, 0.1-0.5 MeV/nucleon Z≥1 ions, 0.4-4 MeV/nucleon heavy ions, and electron channels at 0.1-0.4 and >0.3 MeV

Whitehorse Geophysical Observatory WHS (Whitehorse) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations and magnetic disturbances at the Whitehorse, Yukon observatory, used in auroral-zone/subauroral studies of ionospheric currents, substorms, magnetic bays, pulsations, and geomagnetic storm response

TIMED (Thermosphere Ionosphere Mesosphere Energetics and Dynamics) TIDI (TIMED Doppler Interferometer) Fabry-Perot interferometer measuring mesosphere/lower-thermosphere airglow Doppler shifts and ratios to derive horizontal vector winds, neutral/rotational temperatures, and O2 density; four limb-viewing telescopes observe O I 557.7, 630.0, 844.6 nm, O II 732.0 nm, O2(0-0)/(0-1), Na D, and OH emissions

Pello Geophysical Observatory PEL (Pello) magnetometer, a ground-based three-component fluxgate magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field variations (X/Y/Z or H/D/Z) at the Pello, Finland station; the PEL site in the International Monitor for Auroral Geomagnetic Effects (IMAGE) chain, used for auroral electrojet, substorm, and ultra-low-frequency pulsation studies

Ulysses URAP (Unified Radio and Plasma Waves) radio and plasma-wave investigation measuring solar/Jovian radio emissions, Langmuir/plasma waves, waveforms, and electron density from DC to 1 MHz; comprising RAR (Radio Astronomy Receiver, 1.25-940 kHz), PFR (Plasma Frequency Receiver, 0.57-35 kHz), FES (Fast Envelope Sampler, 10 Hz-60 kHz), WFA (Wave Form Analyzer, DC-500 Hz), and an active sounder

Worthington Geophysical Observatory WRTH (Worthington) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector variations (H/D/Z or X/Y/Z components) and disturbances from ionospheric and magnetospheric currents for space-weather, substorm, and magnetic-pulsation studies

Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer investigation measuring vector magnetic fields in the solar wind, at Jupiter and Saturn, and through the outer heliosphere/heliosheath; uses low-field and high-field sensors with interplanetary accuracy ~0.1 nT and dynamic range ~0.01 nT to 2×10^-3 T

Ulysses LET (Low Energy Telescope) energetic-particle telescope measuring solar energetic particle and cosmic-ray ions—protons, helium, and heavier nuclei—at ~1–20 MeV/nucleon with dE/dx–E pulse-height analysis; one of the five COSPIN (Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation) suite sensors alongside AT (Anisotropy Telescope), HET (High Energy Telescope), HFT (High Flux Telescope), and KET (Kiel Electron Telescope)

Maniitsoq Geophysical Observatory SKT (Sukkertoppen) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations and absolute field at the Greenland west-coast observatory, reported as H/D/Z/F or X/Y/Z components for studies of auroral electrojets, polar-cap convection, geomagnetic storms, and ULF pulsations

Voyager CRS (Cosmic Ray System) energetic-particle telescope suite measuring cosmic-ray and planetary energetic-particle spectra, composition, and anisotropies; comprising HETS (High-Energy Telescope System; Z=1-30 nuclei ~6-500 MeV/nucleon and electrons ~3-100 MeV) and LETS (Low-Energy Telescope System; Z=1-30 nuclei ~0.15-30 MeV/nucleon), including electron telescope measurements of MeV electrons

Tristan da Cunha Geophysical Observatory TDC (Tristan da Cunha) magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic observatory instrument measuring Earth’s magnetic field vector components and temporal variations for solar-terrestrial studies, including magnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, and quiet-day geomagnetic baseline changes

Qaanaaq Geophysical Observatory magnetometer ground-based geomagnetic field instrument measuring three-component magnetic field variations (H/D/Z or X/Y/Z) at the high-latitude Greenland polar-cap station, used for auroral electrojet, ULF pulsation, geomagnetic storm, substorm, and solar-wind/magnetosphere coupling studies; often cited as the Qaanaaq or Thule/Qaanaaq magnetometer.

Kangerlussuaq Geophysical Observatory STF (Søndre Strømfjord/Kangerlussuaq station) ground fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field perturbations and magnetic pulsations in Greenland; reports local H, D, Z or X, Y, Z components for auroral electrojet, field-line resonance, substorm, and ionospheric current studies under the station names Kangerlussuaq, Sondrestromfjord, and STF

Wind STICS (SupraThermal Ion Composition Spectrometer) energetic-particle time-of-flight mass spectrometer measuring suprathermal ion energy, mass, mass/charge, charge-state/composition, and angular distributions from ~6-230 keV/e; one of the three SMS (Solar Wind and Suprathermal Ion Composition) suite sensors alongside SWICS and MASS.

Rorvik Geophysical Observatory MAG (magnetometer) ground-based geomagnetic field instrument measuring local vector magnetic-field variations at Rørvik/Rorvik, Norway, typically reported as horizontal and vertical components (H/D/Z or X/Y/Z) and used for auroral electrojet, substorm, geomagnetic storm, and ULF pulsation studies

Sanikiluaq Geophysical Observatory SNKQ (Sanikiluaq) ground magnetometer measuring three-component geomagnetic field variations and perturbations at the Sanikiluaq, Nunavut station, used in heliophysics papers for auroral electrojet, substorm, field-line resonance, ULF pulsation, and magnetosphere-ionosphere current studies

PENGUIn-4 (Polar Experiment Network for Geospace Upper-atmosphere Investigations) PG4 Geophysical Observatory magnetometer, a ground-based three-component fluxgate geomagnetic field instrument measuring Antarctic magnetic-field variations, ULF pulsations, storm/substorm signatures, and polar ionospheric current disturbances at the PG4 autonomous observatory

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) SHU (Shumagin) ground magnetometer measuring the local geomagnetic field vector and its time variations at the Shumagin station, used for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, ionospheric currents, and regional-to-global geomagnetic disturbance context

Snap Lake Geophysical Observatory SNAP (Snap Lake) magnetometer, a ground-based geomagnetic field instrument measuring vector magnetic field variations and magnetic pulsations at the Snap Lake, Northwest Territories station, reported as local H-D-Z or geographic X-Y-Z components for auroral-zone current systems and space-weather disturbances.

Richardson Geophysical Observatory RICH (Richardson) magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic-field variations and magnetic perturbations, typically reported as vector components such as H/D/Z or north/east/vertical, for studies of auroral electrojets, substorms, magnetic storms, ULF pulsations, and ionospheric current systems at the Richardson ground station

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) YKC (Yellowknife) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector components and temporal variations at Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, Canada; auroral-zone station used for magnetic bays, substorms, Pc pulsations, and geomagnetic disturbance indices

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) OUL (Oulujärvi/Oulujarvi) ground magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field vector components and temporal variations at the Finnish Oulujärvi station, used for studies of auroral electrojets, ionospheric currents, substorms, geomagnetic storms, and ULF magnetic pulsations.

Savissivik Geophysical Observatory SVS (Savissivik) ground magnetometer measuring high-latitude geomagnetic field components and temporal variations at the Greenland observatory, reported under the IAGA station code SVS for studies of ionospheric currents, auroral electrojets, geomagnetic storms, and ULF magnetic pulsations

Ulysses HET (High Energy Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring solar energetic particles and galactic cosmic rays, including H through Fe ions at ~6–600 MeV/n and electron channels at a few–tens of MeV; one of the Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation suite sensors alongside LET (Low Energy Telescope), KET (Kiel Electron Telescope), HFT (High Flux Telescope), and AT (Anisotropy Telescope).

Stanford Geophysical Observatory STFD (Stanford Geophysical Observatory) Stanford Magnetometer ground-based magnetometer measuring local geomagnetic field variations and magnetic perturbations for space-weather, magnetospheric current, storm, substorm, and ultra-low-frequency wave studies at the Stanford station

Petersburg Geophysical Observatory PTRS (Petersburg) magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field strength and time variations at the Petersburg geophysical observatory, providing vector magnetic components used in heliophysics studies of geomagnetic storms, substorms, pulsations, magnetic indices, and solar-wind–magnetosphere coupling at the PTRS station.

TWINS-1 ENA (Energetic Neutral Atom) imager measuring global magnetospheric charge-exchange neutral hydrogen fluxes and ring-current ion distributions at ~1-100 keV; the TWINS-1 unit of the Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers mission package comprises dual wide-angle ENA sensor heads and an LAD (Lyman-alpha Detector) for geocoronal H density correction

Pueblo Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer ground-based magnetometer measuring geomagnetic field variations at the Pueblo, Colorado observatory, providing vector magnetic components commonly reported as H, D, Z or X, Y, Z with total-field F for studies of magnetic storms, substorms, ionospheric currents, and solar-wind–magnetosphere coupling

Ulysses HISCALE (Heliosphere Instrument for Spectra, Composition and Anisotropy at Low Energies) energetic particle instrument measuring electron and ion spectra, anisotropies and composition; comprising LEFS60/LEFS150 (Low Energy Foil Spectrometers), LEMS30/LEMS120 (Low Energy Magnetic Spectrometers) and CA60 (Composition Aperture), covering electrons ~30-300 keV, ions ~50 keV-5 MeV and nuclei ~1-15 MeV/nucleon
